nodes.title: 初始噪声与高层隐式动作
nodes.en: Noise as an Implicit High-Level Action
nodes.summary: 搜索生成器的输入，让它提出接近目标的可达子目标。
nodes.explain:
把DDIM去噪链整体封装成一个函数G：输入当前状态s和初始高斯噪声z，输出未来子目标。现在规划器不直接在所有状态坐标里随意选点，而是在z空间试不同输入，让已学的生成器把这些输入转成候选状态。类似通过旋钮控制一台受训练数据约束的提议机器。这个高层动作不对应某个关节扭矩，也不必是预先训练好的技能编号。搜索过大的异常z仍可能落入模型不熟悉的区域，所以ID-WM额外使用噪声正则。原文把该空间描述得平滑、良态，但神经模型的可达性仍是经验预测，需要低层执行与实验检验。

可固定当前起点，在二维投影里画不同z对应的子目标，再轻微扰动z观察目标如何变化。这能检查局部连续性与覆盖范围，但低维图会隐藏高维问题。最终仍应让低层执行候选，统计哪些子目标确实到达以及在哪里失败。
nodes.symbols: Gθ：完整确定性DDIM映射；zₜ：被规划器优化的初始噪声。
nodes.role: 连接扩散和ID-WM高层CEM：从“生成一个样本”转为“搜索生成器输入”。
nodes.pitfall: z是机器人可以直接执行的动作；高斯输入自动保证任意z都物理有效。
nodes.quiz: 低层仍需做什么？
nodes.answer: 搜索真实动作序列，把当前状态推向高层给出的子目标。

sources.title: ID-WM 原论文：方法与附录

notation.meaning: Initial noise vector for one generated future state.

nodes.definition: When a fixed deterministic generator maps an input noise vector to a candidate future state, selecting that input selects one generated alternative. The input can therefore function as an implicit decision variable. Its coordinates usually lack named physical action meanings. A regular Gaussian input space does not imply that every output is physically valid, nor does it make the generator invertible. Search is needed to find useful input values under the current condition and objective.
nodes.example: Generate twenty candidate future states from twenty noise vectors under the same current-state condition. Evaluate how each candidate advances toward the target and use the better noise vectors to update a CEM proposal distribution. The selected noise is never sent directly to the robot. A separate action-space planner must realize the selected subgoal through the low-level dynamics model.
nodes.role_en: This connects diffusion sampling to ID-WM’s high-level CEM planning. It extends the earlier concept of a generated sample into a searchable decision interface, while the low-level CEM still optimizes executable environment action sequences.
nodes.title_original: 把初始噪声当作高层动作

nodes.title: 训练、推理与测试时规划
nodes.summary: 明确当前被更新的是网络权重，还是动作与噪声候选。
nodes.explain:
训练时拿真实转移做监督，通过反传和优化器更新世界模型权重。部署推理时通常固定权重，但仍可做大量计算：给定候选动作，预测后果，比较目标代价，再改候选。ID-WM还有高层噪声候选的CEM搜索。因此“推理不训练”不表示只运行一次网络，也不表示无需优化。训练损失、单次前向耗时和完整规划延迟衡量的东西不同。若CEM采300个候选、迭代多轮，还在多个时刻重规划，运行成本可远大于一次网络前向。复现时应分别记下数据量、训练更新数、采样步数、候选数量和执行频率。

建议为日志使用不同前缀：train/loss记录拟合，plan/cost记录候选评分，eval/success记录真实环境结果。三者可能同时改善，也可能互相背离。规划器可能利用模型误差得到极低预测代价，却在执行中失败，这时仅追加训练步并不一定解决。
nodes.symbols: θ：世界模型参数；A：动作序列；高层则优化Z噪声序列。
nodes.role: 理解ID-WM的DDPM训练、DDIM生成与双层CEM规划三种计算。
nodes.pitfall: CEM在推理时修改世界模型权重；模型小就保证整套规划实时。
nodes.quiz: 为何固定权重仍可能推理很慢？
nodes.answer: 可能需对大量候选、多次采样和长预测链反复运行网络。

sources.title: ID-WM 原论文：方法与附录

notation.meaning: Test-time action sequence; high-level planning instead searches noise sequence Z.
Training loss and planning objective, respectively.

nodes.definition: Training estimates model parameters from a dataset. Inference evaluates a trained model on new inputs, while test-time planning repeatedly evaluates it to choose decision variables under a goal objective. These processes may all involve computation called optimization, but they optimize different quantities. A large number of planning candidates is not a training batch size, and a diffusion sampling step is not a parameter update. Keeping parameters fixed during planning makes this distinction explicit.
nodes.example: Train a transition model once on recorded state-action-next-state windows. At deployment, keep its weights unchanged and evaluate 300 candidate action sequences toward a new goal. Refitting a CEM proposal changes which actions are considered next, not the transition model itself. A high-level diffusion sampler likewise runs its learned denoiser repeatedly while CEM changes its starting noise sequence.
nodes.role_en: ID-WM combines DDPM-style denoiser training, deterministic DDIM generation, low-level supervised dynamics learning, and two CEM planning searches. This node separates their data, objectives, and optimized variables so the full algorithm can be implemented and timed correctly.
nodes.title_original: 训练、推理与规划时优化

nodes.title: 状态、观察与动作
nodes.summary: 先决定模型到底看见什么、能够做什么。
nodes.explain: 想象桌上有一个圆形推杆和一个 T 形积木。摄像头拍到的 RGB 图像是观察；推杆位置、积木位置和朝向可以组成状态；给推杆的位移指令是动作。图像可能看不到被遮挡的部分，单张图像也通常不能确定速度。因此观察不一定包含未来预测所需的全部信息。工程上要把每个量的单位、坐标系和采样时刻写清楚。ID-WM 文中的 s 还可以表示编码后的特征，不能默认它一定是完整物理状态。
nodes.symbols: x：物理状态；o：传感器观察；s：模型表示；a：动作；t：环境时刻
nodes.role: ID-WM 的输入、目标和两个层级必须采用兼容的状态表示。
nodes.pitfall: 把一张图片当成完全可观测的物理状态。
nodes.quiz: 两张位置相同、运动方向相反的球的照片，未来会相同吗？
nodes.answer: 不会。速度不同；增加历史帧或测量速度可以消除这种歧义。

notation.meaning: Physical state at environment time t.
Representation used by the learned model.

nodes.definition: A physical state contains the information needed to determine the distribution of future states under actions. An observation is a measurement of that state and may omit information. A learned representation encodes observations into features for prediction. These quantities can have different dimensions and should not be used interchangeably.
nodes.example: For PushT, an observation may be an RGB image. A state representation may contain the pusher position and the T-block position and angle. An action can command pusher displacement. Two images with identical positions can correspond to different velocities; a single image may therefore be insufficient for future prediction.
nodes.role_en: ID-WM encodes current and goal observations into compatible representations. Both levels plan using these representations; the action sequence is sent to the environment.

nodes.title: 坐标系与刚体变换
nodes.summary: 同一个位置，必须说明相对谁测量。
nodes.explain: 你站在机器人前面说“球在左边”，机器人自己的左边可能和你的左边相反。坐标系给一组数赋予几何意义。旋转矩阵把方向从一个坐标系转换到另一个，平移向量处理原点不同。对二维 PushT 先学平面位置和角度即可；三维机器人再扩展到旋转矩阵与四元数。角度在 −π 与 π 附近数值不连续，直接相减可能给出错误的距离。
nodes.symbols: pᴮ：B 系中的坐标；Rᴬᴮ：把 B 系向量转到 A 系；tᴬᴮ：B 原点在 A 系中的位置
nodes.role: 机器人迁移扩展；保证状态距离与训练标签的坐标一致。
nodes.pitfall: 混用世界坐标速度和机身坐标速度。
nodes.quiz: 机器人转身后世界坐标固定的球，机身坐标是否会变化？
nodes.answer: 会。坐标表达改变，球本身可以没有移动。

notation.meaning: Coordinates of the same point in frames A and B.
Rotation mapping B-frame vectors to A-frame vectors.
B-frame origin expressed in frame A.

nodes.definition: A reference frame specifies the origin and basis used to express positions and directions. A rigid transformation combines rotation and translation. Coordinate values depend on the chosen frame even when the physical point is fixed. Units, frame conventions and multiplication order must be explicit.
nodes.example: If the frames have the same orientation and the B origin is one metre to the right of the A origin, then a point at zero in B has x-coordinate one in A. A rotating robot can observe changing body-frame ball coordinates even when the ball is stationary.
nodes.role_en: Coordinate consistency is required when constructing robot state labels and goal distances. General 3D rigid transformations are an application extension, not a prerequisite for every state-based ID-WM experiment.

nodes.title: 运动学与动力学
nodes.summary: 姿态几何和受力后的时间变化是不同问题。
nodes.explain: 已知胳膊每个关节的角度，求手在哪里，是运动学。已知当前角度、速度和电机力矩，求下一刻怎么动，是动力学。先用小车理解：位置变化由速度决定，速度变化由加速度决定。学习型世界模型把这些变化从数据中拟合出来，也必须面对接触、摩擦和未观察变量。机器人全身模型的困难常来自碰撞与接触切换，而不只是坐标有三个维度。
nodes.symbols: q：位置或关节角；v：速度；u：输入；F：一步动力学
nodes.role: 解释 ID-WM 为什么需要动作条件的低层模型；G1 扩展需单独处理动力学和接触。
nodes.pitfall: 用静态姿态重建成功证明动态控制成功。
nodes.quiz: 知道关节角就能唯一预测下一刻姿态吗？
nodes.answer: 通常不能，还需要速度、动作、接触等相关信息。
nodes.definition: Kinematics relates configurations to geometric quantities such as end-effector position. Dynamics describes how state evolves under inputs and forces. A discrete dynamics model predicts the next state from the current state and action. Contact, friction and omitted variables can make this mapping difficult to learn.
nodes.example: A one-dimensional constant-velocity model with time step 0.02 seconds and velocity 1 metre per second predicts a displacement of 0.02 metres. If a control changes velocity, position alone no longer specifies the next state; velocity and relevant inputs are required.
nodes.role_en: The low-level world model learns action-conditioned transitions. Robot applications additionally require appropriate contact states and action interfaces; the paper does not establish full-body G1 performance.

nodes.title: 马尔可夫性与历史窗口
nodes.summary: 保留足够的信息，才能预测未来。
nodes.explain: 如果当前状态已经包含位置和速度，理想小车的下一步通常不需要知道昨天在哪里，这就是马尔可夫建模的直觉。若只给位置，过去两帧的位置差能够帮助估计速度。用历史窗口是补充信息的一种办法，但有限窗口不保证完全恢复隐藏状态。ID-WM 低层读取过去若干状态和动作；工程上要检查序列切片是否跨越重置边界，以及目标帧有没有意外进入输入。
nodes.symbols: k：历史窗口长度；p：条件概率
nodes.role: 理解低层 Transformer 的上下文输入和部分可观测问题。
nodes.pitfall: 把增加历史长度当成必然解决遮挡和隐藏变量。
nodes.quiz: 只有球位置的观测，最少还想补什么信息？
nodes.answer: 速度，或足以估计速度的相邻历史观测；噪声下可能需要更长窗口。

notation.meaning: Number of previous time steps retained.
States from index i through j.

nodes.definition: A Markov state makes the future conditionally independent of earlier history once the current state and action are given. When observations omit relevant variables, a finite history can supply additional information. A history window is an approximation and does not guarantee complete observability.
nodes.example: Two successive positions allow an estimate of velocity using position difference divided by elapsed time. With only one position, opposite velocities remain possible. Window construction must stop at episode boundaries; the reset state of another episode is not a valid next observation.
nodes.role_en: ID-WM low-level prediction uses histories of states and actions. Window length determines input context, not the number of future planning steps.
nodes.title_original: 马尔可夫性与历史窗口

nodes.title: 开环、反馈与执行闭环
nodes.summary: 边走边看，修正预测误差。
nodes.explain: 闭眼按预先写好的路线走十步，是开环；走一步看一次位置再调整，是反馈。模型误差和外界扰动会让开环轨迹逐渐偏离。反馈控制把实际观察重新带回决策。重新规划也有成本：频率更高可能反应更及时，却需要更多计算。ID-WM 规划出的子目标不能当成已经真实到达的状态，执行后仍要读取环境实际观察。
nodes.symbols: π：决策规则；g：目标；o₀:ₜ：到当前的观察历史
nodes.role: 连接世界模型的想象轨迹和真实环境执行。
nodes.pitfall: 把模型想象成功等同于机器人执行成功。
nodes.quiz: 有风的小车按预测动作走偏了，下一步应从哪个状态规划？
nodes.answer: 从重新测得或估计的实际状态出发。
nodes.definition: Open-loop execution applies a planned input sequence without using new measurements to change it. Feedback uses measured or estimated state to revise subsequent control. Feedback can reduce the effect of disturbances and model error, but its effectiveness depends on observation quality, delay and available actions.
nodes.example: A pusher executes a movement and the block slips less than predicted. A feedback controller measures the resulting position and updates its next action. Continuing to use the original imagined block position would ignore the execution error.
nodes.role_en: ID-WM observes the actual state after executing low-level plans and replans according to its execution schedule. An imagined rollout is not evidence that the real environment reached the same states.

nodes.title: 目标、代价与约束
nodes.summary: 告诉规划器什么算好，什么必须满足。
nodes.explain: 推积木时，可以用最终位置误差表示离目标还有多远；但位置近并不保证积木角度对，推杆也可能没有到位。代价是越小越好的评分，约束是必须满足的限制，例如动作幅度上限。给不同维度加权相当于规定厘米误差与角度误差的重要性。学习表征里的欧氏距离是否对应任务成功，需要用真实任务指标检验。
nodes.symbols: A：动作序列；H：预测长度；d：状态距离；λ：权重；此式为教学通用形式
nodes.role: 论文规划使用目标距离与高层噪声正则；不要将教学动作代价误认为原文公式。
nodes.pitfall: 忽略量纲，直接把米和弧度的数值相加。
nodes.quiz: 位置重合但积木朝向相反，能直接判定成功吗？
nodes.answer: 不能。成功判据必须包含任务要求的朝向或覆盖率等量。

notation.meaning: Action-penalty weight in this general teaching example.

nodes.definition: A goal specifies a desired outcome. A cost assigns a scalar score to a candidate plan, while constraints restrict admissible plans. Different state components may require different scales or weights. The displayed action penalty is a general control example, not an additional term claimed for the ID-WM paper.
nodes.example: If block position matches the target but its orientation is reversed, position error alone can be zero while the task remains incomplete. A suitable goal representation or success criterion must include the relevant orientation or overlap requirement.
nodes.role_en: ID-WM scores predicted goal distance. Its high-level objective also penalizes selected noise values. Costs and success metrics must be distinguished.

nodes.title: 多步推演与误差累积
nodes.summary: 把自己的预测再喂回模型，错误会传播。
nodes.explain: 一步预测误差很小的模型，连续预测很多步仍可能失败。比如每步位置偏一点，下一步就从偏掉的位置继续计算；接触是否发生还可能因此改变，造成更大的分岔。下面的不等式是示意：局部误差 δ 与系统对输入误差的放大程度 L 共同决定长期误差。它说明为什么必须测多步推演，不能只汇报一步均方误差。分层与反馈都能改变问题结构，但不会使误差消失。
nodes.formula: eₜ₊₁ ≤ L eₜ + δ （局部误差传播示意）
nodes.symbols: e：状态预测误差；L：局部敏感程度；δ：单步模型误差
nodes.role: ID-WM 解决长时域规划的核心动机之一。
nodes.pitfall: 认为一步误差降低一半就保证任务成功率翻倍。
nodes.quiz: 什么时候小误差会导致完全不同的后续轨迹？
nodes.answer: 接触切换、障碍物边界或不稳定动力学附近，误差可能被显著放大。

notation.meaning: Predicted state, reused as the next input.
Local error amplification and one-step model error in an illustrative bound.

nodes.definition: A rollout repeatedly applies a transition model to predict a state sequence. Errors affect later predictions because predicted states become subsequent inputs. Near contact transitions, small state errors can change whether a collision occurs. A one-step prediction metric does not fully characterize long-horizon reliability.
nodes.example: A one-step positional bias of one millimetre can accumulate over repeated predictions. With contact, the error can alter the contact event itself, so later error need not grow linearly. Evaluate rollout error at several horizons and compare actual execution.
nodes.role_en: Compounding error is a central motivation for the ID-WM hierarchy. Local prediction, subgoal organization and feedback address different parts of the problem.

nodes.title: 搜索空间与组合爆炸
nodes.summary: 动作选项和时间长度一起放大搜索难度。
nodes.explain: 假设每一步只选左、右、上、下四个动作，十步就有 4¹⁰ 种序列。连续动作不是有限枚举，但维数仍随时域增长：每步 d 个数，H 步共有 H×d 个待优化量。穷举很快不可行，于是使用随机采样、优化与层级抽象。分层让高层先选择几个中途地点，低层处理局部控制；它减少某些搜索困难，同时增加了子目标可执行性这一要求。
nodes.formula: 离散候选数 bᴴ；连续决策维数 H·dₐ
nodes.symbols: b：每步候选动作数；H：步数；dₐ：动作维数
nodes.role: 解释 ID-WM 高层搜索噪声、低层搜索动作的设计动机。
nodes.pitfall: 把搜索算法最坏情况复杂度直接当成实际运行时间。
nodes.quiz: 每步 2 维动作、规划 20 步，序列含多少标量？
nodes.answer: 40 个标量；这还没有算候选轨迹数量。

notation.meaning: Number of discrete action choices at each step.

nodes.definition: Planning searches over candidate decisions. Discrete sequence counts can grow exponentially with horizon; continuous action optimization has a decision dimension proportional to horizon. Sample count, search iterations and model evaluation cost jointly determine practical runtime.
nodes.example: Four choices per step produce 1,048,576 possible sequences over ten steps. For two-dimensional continuous actions and twenty steps, a candidate sequence contains forty scalar decision variables before accounting for the number of candidates.
nodes.role_en: ID-WM separates high-level noise-sequence search from local action-sequence search. This changes the organization of the search rather than eliminating its computation.

nodes.title: 随机射击规划
nodes.summary: 先随机试很多条计划，再选最好的一条。
nodes.explain: 你可以先生成 100 条不同的推杆动作序列，在模型里分别试跑，给每条末端误差打分，再执行最优的一条。这就是随机射击的基本流程。它不需要对模型求导，便于处理难以微分的代价，但好轨迹在大空间里可能极少。它是理解 CEM 的起点：CEM 会利用当前较好的样本，调整下一轮从哪里采样。
nodes.symbols: N：候选数；A⁽ⁱ⁾：第 i 个动作序列；J：代价
nodes.role: CEM 规划的算法先修。
nodes.pitfall: 采样最多的方案必然在所有任务中最优。
nodes.quiz: 随机射击与训练模型的参数更新是否相同？
nodes.answer: 不同。射击在推理时挑选动作，训练改变模型权重。

sources.title: CEM 与梯度规划原论文

nodes.definition: Random shooting samples complete candidate action sequences, predicts their outcomes and returns the lowest-cost candidate. The procedure is derivative-free. Its performance depends on the sampling distribution and budget, especially when successful sequences occupy a small part of the search space.
nodes.example: Sample one hundred pusher sequences and predict the final block state for each. Compute its distance to the target and choose the smallest. The network weights remain fixed while candidate actions vary.
nodes.role_en: Random shooting supplies the basic sample-evaluate-select structure that CEM improves by adapting the next sampling distribution.

nodes.title: 交叉熵方法：采样—精英—重拟合
nodes.summary: 让下一轮尝试集中在较好的候选附近。
nodes.explain: 先给每个待优化数设置均值和标准差，从高斯分布采一批候选。用模型推演并打分，留下代价最低的一小批“精英”。用精英计算新的均值和方差，再重复。比如推杆应向右移动约 0.3，第一轮散布在各方向，精英集中在向右附近，下一轮就在该区域密集探索。方差过早变小会失去探索，因此实现常设方差下界或平滑更新。CEM 的名字与交叉熵有关，实际循环可以先从采样和拟合学会。
nodes.symbols: μ、σ²：逐维采样参数；elite：按代价选出的精英；优化变量也可换成 Z
nodes.role: ID-WM 高层和低层均采用 CEM；高层优化 Z，低层优化 A。
nodes.pitfall: 把 CEM 当成神经网络的一种层或把精英比例当成功率。
nodes.quiz: 高层与低层的 CEM 分别在修改什么？
nodes.answer: 高层修改生成子目标的噪声序列 Z；低层修改可执行动作序列 A。

sources.title: CEM 与梯度规划原论文

notation.meaning: Candidate decision vector; an action sequence or noise sequence.
Elite index set and number of elites.
Coordinate-wise mean and variance of the sampling distribution.

nodes.definition: The Cross-Entropy Method repeatedly samples decisions, evaluates cost, selects a low-cost elite subset and fits a new proposal distribution to that subset. The displayed diagonal-Gaussian update uses empirical means and variances. Practical implementations may smooth updates or impose a minimum variance to avoid premature concentration.
nodes.example: To minimize a squared distance to three, sample sixty scalar candidates from a broad Gaussian, retain ten with smallest cost, and update the mean and variance using those ten. Repeating the operation usually concentrates samples near three; it does not guarantee a global optimum in arbitrary objectives.
nodes.role_en: ID-WM uses CEM at both levels. High-level decision vectors contain initial diffusion noise; low-level decision vectors contain executable actions.
nodes.title_original: 交叉熵方法：采样—精英—重拟合

nodes.title: 模型预测控制
nodes.summary: 预测一段未来，执行后用新观察重新规划。
nodes.explain: 从当前状态出发，规划未来 H 步，执行一部分，再观察实际状态，重复这一循环，就是 MPC 的核心。它把有限计算预算持续分配给当前问题。经典实现常只执行第一个动作，实际系统也可以按块执行；ID-WM 的算法按子目标执行低层计划，再更新实际状态，完成一轮高层计划后重新规划。阅读论文时要明确其执行和重规划粒度，不能把所有 MPC 都画成同一种逐帧循环。
nodes.formula: 观察 → 预测候选 → 最小化代价 → 执行动作块 → 再观察
nodes.symbols: H：每次前看的有限时域；动作块长度影响闭环反应与算力
nodes.role: ID-WM 的推理总体框架。
nodes.pitfall: 认为每次重新规划意味着重新训练网络。
nodes.quiz: 环境执行后的状态偏离想象，MPC 为什么还有机会修正？
nodes.answer: 后续规划从新观察出发，而不一直沿用旧的预测起点。

notation.meaning: Newly observed or estimated state at planning time.
Number of actions executed before the next observation/update.

nodes.definition: Model Predictive Control repeatedly solves a finite-horizon planning problem, executes part of the selected plan and updates the initial state from new observations. Execution granularity varies by implementation. The classic one-action receding-horizon case is not the only valid schedule.
nodes.example: A controller plans five actions, executes two, measures the resulting state and plans again. If the measured state differs from the predicted state, the next optimization starts from the measurement. Planning changes decisions; it need not retrain model weights.
nodes.role_en: ID-WM organizes high-level subgoal search and low-level realization in an execution loop. The paper specifies action-block and high-level replanning schedules.

nodes.title: 可达性与流形
nodes.summary: 看起来接近的状态，可能无法在短时间内到达。
nodes.explain: 墙两侧的点在直线距离上很近，但机器人必须绕过门才能过去。可达性询问在动力学、动作限制和时间预算下能否到达。流形可以先理解为高维空间中符合约束的一片结构：二维地图里的合法点避开墙，机械臂合法姿态还受关节和接触限制。训练数据只能提供有限覆盖，生成模型学到的可达结构是一种经验近似，不能提供所有状态的物理可达保证。
nodes.formula: R_Δ(s) = {s′：存在允许的动作使 s 在 Δ 步内到 s′}
nodes.symbols: R_Δ：Δ 步可达集合；Δ：时间预算；此式为概念定义
nodes.role: 高层模型学习局部未来状态分布；低层仍需验证子目标能否实现。
nodes.pitfall: 把每个生成样本都视为有形式证明的可达状态。
nodes.quiz: 隔墙两个点距离短，为什么仍需多个子目标？
nodes.answer: 合法路径受障碍物和动力学约束，需要绕行。

notation.meaning: Set of states reachable from s within the stated budget.
Transition under dynamics and admissible actions.

nodes.definition: Reachability concerns whether a state can be attained under dynamics, action limits and environmental constraints within a specified time. A data manifold describes structured states represented in training data. A learned approximation to this structure does not provide a formal guarantee that every generated state is physically reachable.
nodes.example: Two positions on opposite sides of a wall can be close in Euclidean distance, yet require a long path through a doorway. If the time budget is too short, the second position is not reachable even though its coordinates are nearby.
nodes.role_en: The high-level model estimates distributions of local future states. Its predictions must remain compatible with what the low-level controller can realize.

nodes.title: 策略、价值与强化学习
nodes.summary: 理解规划方法与直接策略方法的关系。
nodes.explain: 策略把观察变成动作，价值函数评估一个状态或动作在长期上有多好。强化学习通常利用奖励改进策略。世界模型可以作为强化学习中的一部分，也可以独立用于目标规划。ID-WM 从无奖励标注的离线转移数据学习动力学，再在测试时按目标距离规划；理解 MDP 很有用，但读懂主方法不必先实现 PPO。价值学习这一分支帮助理解论文对 HIQL 等基线的比较。
nodes.symbols: π：策略；V：价值；r：奖励；γ：折扣因子
nodes.role: 背景比较分支；ID-WM 核心不依赖先训练一个任务奖励策略。
nodes.pitfall: 把 world model、策略和价值函数混成同一个输出动作的网络。
nodes.quiz: 预测下一状态的网络是否已经是一条策略？
nodes.answer: 没有。还需要根据目标选择动作的机制，例如规划器。
nodes.latex: a\sim\pi(\cdot\mid s),\qquad V^\pi(s)=\mathbb E_\pi\!\left[\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}\gamma^t r_t\mid s_0=s\right]

notation.meaning: Expected discounted return under the policy.

nodes.definition: A policy selects actions from observations or states. A value function estimates future return under a policy. Reinforcement learning improves decisions using reward-related objectives. A world model predicts transitions and can support planning without learning a task-specific reward policy.
nodes.example: A next-state predictor can evaluate the consequence of moving left, but does not by itself decide whether left is desirable. A planner compares consequences against a goal, while a policy directly returns an action.
nodes.role_en: Policy and value concepts support comparison with goal-conditioned imitation and hierarchical RL baselines. Implementing PPO is not necessary to understand ID-WM core planning.

nodes.title: 离线数据、分布外与模型利用
nodes.summary: 规划器会主动寻找模型可能出错的地方。
nodes.explain: 离线数据是事先记录的状态—动作—后续状态，不会自动覆盖规划器日后提出的所有尝试。一个模型可能在常见动作上准确，却对极端动作产生“穿墙”的假象。优化器只看到代价，可能偏爱这些假象，这叫模型利用。测试时目标没见过，不等于所有物理环境都能泛化。可以通过动作限制、噪声正则、分布外检查、多步真实执行验证来减轻问题，但不能将这些措施当作完备保证。
nodes.formula: 训练分布 D_train ≠ 规划诱导分布 D_plan
nodes.symbols: OOD：out of distribution，分布外；分布差异不一定能只用一个数概括
nodes.role: 解释 ID-WM 为什么给噪声设置正则、为什么要做真实环境闭环评测。
nodes.pitfall: 把测试目标未见过说成无需数据也能处理任意环境。
nodes.quiz: 为什么模型误差可能在优化后反而更严重？
nodes.answer: 优化器会选择预测有利的区域，其中可能包含训练覆盖不足导致的系统性错误。

notation.meaning: Distribution induced by planning and execution.
Learned transition model used for cost evaluation.

nodes.definition: Offline model learning uses previously recorded transitions. Planning may select actions or states poorly covered by those records. Model exploitation occurs when an optimizer prefers predictions that look beneficial because of model error, rather than because the real system can achieve them.
nodes.example: A predictor trained on ordinary pusher movements may incorrectly predict that an extreme movement crosses a wall. An optimizer can select this error because the imagined endpoint is close to the goal. Checking only random held-out transitions may miss the failure.
nodes.role_en: ID-WM regularizes high-level noise to discourage extreme search inputs and evaluates closed-loop performance. These measures reduce selected risks without proving universal out-of-distribution reliability.
nodes.title_original: 离线数据、分布外与模型利用

nodes.title: ID-WM：全方法总览
nodes.summary: 先规划去哪里，再求怎么走过去。
nodes.explain: 继续用推 T 形积木的例子：只看终点，连续搜索几百步动作非常困难。ID-WM 用一个高层模型从当前状态生成若干局部未来可能性，规划器挑出一串中途状态。随后低层模型帮助搜索真正能够推动推杆的动作。执行后读取真实状态继续规划。高层和低层是两个模型，规划器是搜索过程；它们共同形成算法。核心学习目标来自离线转移数据，推理时才给出具体目标。这里的世界模型主要服务于状态与表征空间规划，不能将其等同于大型视频生成游戏。
nodes.symbols: θ、φ：两个模型参数；z：高层隐式决策；a：环境动作；i：高层索引；t：低层时间
nodes.role: 终点节点：把数学、生成建模与控制三条主线汇合。
nodes.pitfall: 把高层生成的目标直接发送给电机。
nodes.quiz: 给出当前状态与目标后，哪些量在推理时被搜索，哪些一般固定？
nodes.answer: 搜索高层 Z 和低层 A；训练好的模型权重一般固定。

notation.meaning: High-level noise decision and environment action.
High-level index and environment/model time index.

nodes.definition: ID-WM is a hierarchical planning method that separates local future-state generation from action realization. A diffusion-based high-level model proposes subgoals. A low-level forward model evaluates candidate action sequences to reach those subgoals. Both are learned from offline transitions; goals are supplied for planning at test time.
nodes.example: In PushT, a high-level plan proposes a sequence of pusher-and-block configurations. Low-level CEM searches movements that approach the next configuration. After action execution the algorithm reads the actual state and continues according to the planning schedule.
nodes.role_en: This is the integration point for representations, conditional diffusion, CEM, local dynamics and execution feedback. The experiments concern state/feature-space planning, not a general video game renderer.

paper.contribution: Composes local reachable-state generation with low-level action planning for long-horizon goal reaching.

architecture.label: Observation representation
architecture.role: Encode current and goal observations into compatible state or feature representations.

architecture.label: High-level diffusion generator
architecture.role: Map current state and selected initial noise to a local future state.

architecture.label: High-level and low-level CEM
architecture.role: Search noise sequences for subgoals and action sequences for execution.

architecture.label: Action-conditioned forward model
architecture.role: Predict candidate local outcomes from state and action histories.

architecture.label: Execution feedback
architecture.role: Read actual observations after action blocks and replan according to the algorithm.

paper.training: Offline state pairs train the high-level denoiser; action-conditioned temporal windows train the low-level next-state predictor. Task rewards are not required for these dynamics objectives.
paper.inference: CEM first searches diffusion-noise sequences for subgoals, then searches executable actions using low-level forward rollouts. Real execution updates the observed state.
paper.evaluation: Wall, PushT and Maze suites. Success, object coverage, prediction quality, planning budgets and ablations belong to this paper record, not separate graph nodes.
paper.scale: State-based low-level configuration reports a six-layer Transformer with eight heads. The full system parameter count is not explicitly summarized; visual experiments use a different backbone. Depth is not parameter count.
paper.limitations: Finite offline coverage, model exploitation, subgoal executability and repeated planning cost remain relevant. Navigation/manipulation evidence does not establish humanoid soccer performance.
paper.evidence_level: Public research paper and project demonstrations; no reproduction claim by this atlas.

sections.definition: The high-level world model learns a conditional distribution of local future states from pairs of states separated in time. It does not directly output the detailed action sequence between those states. Conditional generation can represent multiple plausible future configurations.
sections.example: From a state near a doorway, recorded trajectories may include turning left or right. A deterministic average can lie in an invalid region; a conditional generative model can produce distinct future alternatives. The low-level planner must then determine which alternatives it can execute.
sections.role_en: The model implements ID-WM local reachability abstraction. Training coverage and low-level planning budget limit what its generated subgoals can reliably support.

sections.definition: With fixed model parameters, conditioning state and deterministic DDIM settings, initial noise is mapped to a generated future state. Planning can therefore optimize noise vectors as implicit high-level actions. Individual noise coordinates need not have a direct physical interpretation.
sections.example: Hold the current state fixed and use two different noise vectors. The generator may produce different local future configurations. CEM evaluates chains of such configurations by goal distance. The selected noise is an input to the generator, not a command sent to a robot actuator.
sections.role_en: This connects high-level generative modeling to derivative-free decision search. A regular input space does not guarantee that every generated transition is physically valid.

sections.definition: The low-level model is trained as an action-conditioned forward predictor using state-action histories. It supports inverse planning by rolling out candidate action sequences and selecting those that reach a specified target. The inverse computation is performed by search rather than requiring a separate direct inverse-dynamics network.
sections.example: Given a block subgoal, CEM samples pusher movements. The forward model predicts the final state for each movement sequence. The sequence with the smallest subgoal distance is selected. The displayed training norm follows the paper; squared MSE is a related but distinct objective.
sections.role_en: ID-WM uses a Transformer predictor and an MLP action encoder for this level. The model supplies predictions; CEM supplies action selection.

sections.definition: The high-level objective combines predicted terminal distance with a penalty on noise coordinates whose magnitude exceeds a threshold. This discourages optimization from using extreme inputs outside typical training conditions. The penalty is not the exact Gaussian negative log likelihood and does not prove collision avoidance or physical feasibility.
sections.example: For threshold two, exponent one and a noise coordinate equal to three, the unaveraged penalty contribution is one. A coordinate of magnitude one contributes zero. Aggregate contributions as defined and multiply by the regularization weight before adding goal distance.
sections.role_en: The paper equations (5) and (6) couple goal search to prior-aware noise control. Weight and threshold choices should be evaluated with ablations.

sections.definition: Temporal abstraction organizes a task into transitions over a coarser time scale. ID-WM composes local generated states into a subgoal chain and uses local action search to realize its transitions. High-level horizon, local training interval, low-level action horizon and environment frame skip are separate configuration choices.
sections.example: A long route through a maze can be specified by several intermediate states, each reachable by local control. Moving all subgoals farther apart can make local execution fail. Structural lookahead can grow through composition without guaranteeing an exact execution duration.
sections.role_en: The hierarchy extends local modeling to long-horizon search and is evaluated against flat world-model planning. Compatibility between high- and low-level time scales is essential.

sections.definition: Training constructs targets from offline trajectories and updates model parameters. Inference receives current and goal observations and searches decisions with the learned models. Execution then produces new observations for subsequent planning. Candidate count and search iterations are inference budgets, distinct from training epochs and optimization steps.
sections.example: Changing the requested goal changes the planning objective and selected decisions. Within the learned environment coverage it need not require retraining both models. Using future test-trajectory states as model input would leak information and invalidate the claimed planning evaluation.
sections.role_en: This describes the paper execution dataflow. Implementations must specify context slicing, episode resets, action-block execution, stopping conditions and maximum replans.

sections.definition: Method comparison should identify prediction targets, decision variables, training data and additional dependencies. DINO-WM supplies action-conditioned feature prediction and planning. ID-WM adds a high-level local-future generator. Diffuser models trajectories with diffusion, while ID-WM uses diffusion for local future-state generation and composes outcomes through search.
sections.example: Two methods can both use diffusion yet generate different objects: one generates a complete trajectory, another generates a neighboring state. Their sampling procedures and success criteria cannot be equated from the shared term alone.
sections.role_en: These are methodological connections rather than mathematical prerequisites. Hierarchical policy/value baselines provide comparisons with different assumptions about task supervision.

sections.definition: Evaluation measures outcomes under specified initial conditions, goals, data and planning budgets. Success rate and object coverage capture different aspects of completion. Ablations alter a selected component while controlling other relevant settings. Relative gain must be distinguished from percentage-point difference.
sections.example: A change from twenty percent success to forty-seven percent is a twenty-seven percentage-point increase and a one-hundred-thirty-five percent relative gain. One visually successful rollout does not determine a success rate or establish generalization.
sections.role_en: The paper evaluates Wall, PushT and Maze tasks with defined data and goal settings. These results are not direct evidence of physical humanoid or robot-soccer performance.

sections.definition: An ID-WM reproduction must fix paper version, data splits, environment, model settings and planning budget. Verify startup, prediction quality and closed-loop task outcomes separately. Timing must state which stages are included and account for asynchronous accelerator execution.
sections.example: Two planners can have equal candidate counts yet different runtimes because one repeatedly invokes diffusion sampling. Report both task success and measured wall-clock latency. A video played at twenty-four frames per second does not establish a twenty-four-hertz planner.
sections.role_en: This paper-specific implementation section guides evidence collection. It distinguishes a runnable training script from completed training and validated reproduction.

sections.definition: These milestones are an implementation plan for ID-WM. Start with isolated state-based components, measure each component, then integrate the hierarchy. Add visual representations after separating dynamics and planning failures. The sequence is a teaching recommendation rather than an author-provided reproduction benchmark.
sections.example: First fit synthetic one-step state transitions and check them numerically. Next implement CEM and closed-loop MPC on a small state environment. Then learn conditional future-state samples and search their initial noise. Finally connect high- and low-level models and evaluate unseen start-goal pairs before adding images.
sections.role_en: Each milestone should produce saved configurations, held-out metrics and failure trajectories. Completing a simplified teaching environment is not equivalent to reproducing the paper.

nodes.title: Python 与数组编程
nodes.summary: 把数学中的一串数落实为可检查的数据。
nodes.explain: 从列表、循环、函数开始，再学习数组的形状和逐元素运算。比如一批轨迹形状是 [B,T,D]：B 条片段、每条 T 个时间步、每步 D 个特征。切片 x[:, :-1] 与 x[:, 1:] 构造相邻训练对。广播可以减少循环，但也会悄悄把两个错误形状组合成一个巨大的数组；每一步都写出预期形状。代码应从小的、可以手算的样本起步，而不是直接训练巨型模型。
nodes.symbols: B：批大小；T：时间长度；D：特征维数
nodes.role: 实现数据处理、CEM 候选批次与学习循环的基础。
nodes.pitfall: 把 Python 列表相加误认为向量数值相加。
nodes.quiz: [2,3] 的列表加法与数组逐元素加法有什么区别？
nodes.answer: 列表加法拼接；数值数组可以得到逐元素和，须确认对象类型。
nodes.latex: X\in\mathbb R^{B\times T\times D},\qquad X_{\mathrm{in}}=X_{:,0:T-1,:},\quad X_{\mathrm{target}}=X_{:,1:T,:}

notation.meaning: Batch size, sequence length and feature dimension.
All entries along that array axis in the slicing notation.

nodes.definition: Array programming represents numerical data with explicitly ordered axes. Operations such as indexing, slicing, broadcasting and matrix multiplication must respect those axes and the meaning of each feature. A mathematically valid array operation can still be an incorrect data transformation.
nodes.example: A batch of eight trajectories, each with ten time steps and four features, has shape eight by ten by four. Adjacent input-target windows each contain nine time steps. Python list addition concatenates lists; numerical array addition adds corresponding elements under its broadcasting rules.
nodes.role_en: These skills implement trajectory preparation and batched planning. Preserve coordinate, unit and episode-boundary information alongside array shapes.

nodes.title: PyTorch 训练最小闭环
nodes.summary: 数据进入模型，损失反传，优化器更新。
nodes.explain: 一个训练步的顺序是清梯度、前向计算、算损失、反向传播、更新参数。自动微分记录张量运算图，替你应用链式法则，但不会自动检查标签含义。推理时设置 eval 并在适合场景关闭梯度；训练中的 dropout 等行为可能不同。先在几十个合成样本上验证损失下降和预测正确，再使用真实轨迹。看到 GPU 在运行只能说明计算启动，不能说明模型学会任务。
nodes.symbols: loss：标量目标；grad：参数梯度；optimizer：更新规则
nodes.role: 可以实现低层监督训练与扩散噪声预测训练。
nodes.pitfall: 遗漏清梯度、把目标张量对齐错一步、在训练中误 detach。
nodes.quiz: loss.backward() 是否已经修改了模型权重？
nodes.answer: 通常只计算/累积梯度；optimizer.step() 才更新参数。

notation.meaning: Parameter gradient computed by automatic differentiation.

nodes.definition: A PyTorch training step clears old gradients, computes predictions and loss, differentiates the loss, then updates parameters. Automatic differentiation applies the chain rule to recorded tensor operations; it does not verify target alignment or task semantics. Evaluation mode and disabled gradient recording serve different purposes.
nodes.example: Calling backward computes or accumulates parameter gradients. The optimizer step subsequently changes weights. If the target trajectory is shifted by an extra time step, the code may run and loss may decrease while fitting the wrong prediction task.
nodes.role_en: The high-level denoising loss and low-level transition loss can both be implemented with this pattern. GPU activity alone does not demonstrate learning or task success.

nodes.title: 轨迹切片与防止时间泄漏
nodes.summary: 同一段未来不能通过另一扇门进入训练输入。
nodes.explain: 轨迹数据有连续时间相关性。如果把所有帧打乱再分训练测试，邻近的几乎相同画面可能同时出现，两边指标会虚高。通常按 episode、场景或采集批次划分，再在各集合内部切片。每个窗口应含历史、动作与未来标签，并排除跨 reset 的窗口。高层状态对还要保证 Δ 没越过 episode 末尾。保存随机种子和索引清单，便于后来复现同一评价。
nodes.symbols: reset：一次任务结束后的重置；泄漏：测试信息进入训练流程
nodes.role: 两个世界模型共用的数据质量基础。
nodes.pitfall: 按帧随机切分就宣称跨轨迹泛化。
nodes.quiz: 跨 episode 取最后一帧与下一 episode 第一帧作转移会怎样？
nodes.answer: 制造不存在的动力学跳跃，模型会学到错误标签。
nodes.definition: Trajectory dataset construction divides episodes or other independent collection units before constructing temporal windows. History, action and target indices must align. Windows must not cross resets, and test information must not enter training through near-duplicate adjacent frames or preprocessing fitted on test data.
nodes.example: If an episode ends at time ninety-nine, a target offset of five is invalid for a window starting at time ninety-eight. Taking frames from the next reset episode creates a transition that never physically occurred.
nodes.role_en: Both ID-WM levels depend on correct temporal pairing. Dataset manifests and fixed split indices make experiments reproducible.
nodes.title_original: 轨迹切片与防止时间泄漏

nodes.title: 定积分
nodes.summary: A definite integral accumulates a function over an interval, using a limit of weighted sums when that limit exists.
nodes.definition: A definite integral accumulates a function over an interval, using a limit of weighted sums when that limit exists. The variable of integration specifies which quantity changes across the interval. Signed values may cancel, so an integral is not always geometric area. Physical interpretation depends on units: integrating velocity over time gives displacement, while integrating a probability density over an event gives probability.
nodes.example: A constant velocity of two metres per second over three seconds gives six metres of displacement. If velocity becomes negative during part of the interval, integrate the signed velocity to obtain displacement; integrating speed instead gives total distance travelled. State the interval explicitly.
nodes.role_en: Integrals connect continuous dynamics, trajectory costs, probability densities and expected quantities. They are foundational for simulation and control, even when a learned discrete world model never evaluates an analytic integral explicitly.

notation.meaning: Sample in interval i and interval width.

nodes.explain: A definite integral accumulates a function over an interval, using a limit of weighted sums when that limit exists. The variable of integration specifies which quantity changes across the interval. Signed values may cancel, so an integral is not always geometric area. Physical interpretation depends on units: integrating velocity over time gives displacement, while integrating a probability density over an event gives probability.
nodes.role: Integrals connect continuous dynamics, trajectory costs, probability densities and expected quantities. They are foundational for simulation and control, even when a learned discrete world model never evaluates an analytic integral explicitly.

nodes.title: 微积分基本定理
nodes.summary: The fundamental theorem links differentiation and integration under suitable regularity assumptions.
nodes.definition: The fundamental theorem links differentiation and integration under suitable regularity assumptions. The derivative of an accumulation function equals its continuous integrand. Conversely, a definite integral can be evaluated by subtracting endpoint values of an antiderivative. These statements justify converting known rates into state changes and checking a proposed analytic trajectory by differentiation. Their assumptions matter for discontinuities and impulses arising in contact dynamics.
nodes.example: If acceleration is constant at three metres per second squared, velocity changes by six metres per second over two seconds. Differentiating the resulting linear velocity trajectory recovers the acceleration; this check verifies both the coefficient and the time units. This also checks sign conventions.
nodes.role_en: This theorem connects physical rates to integrated trajectories. Contact impulses require separate treatment rather than applying a smooth acceleration formula across an instantaneous velocity jump.

notation.meaning: An antiderivative of f under the theorem assumptions.

nodes.explain: The fundamental theorem links differentiation and integration under suitable regularity assumptions. The derivative of an accumulation function equals its continuous integrand. Conversely, a definite integral can be evaluated by subtracting endpoint values of an antiderivative. These statements justify converting known rates into state changes and checking a proposed analytic trajectory by differentiation. Their assumptions matter for discontinuities and impulses arising in contact dynamics.
nodes.role: This theorem connects physical rates to integrated trajectories. Contact impulses require separate treatment rather than applying a smooth acceleration formula across an instantaneous velocity jump.

nodes.title: 泰勒展开
nodes.summary: A Taylor approximation expresses how a function changes near a specified input using derivatives at that input.
nodes.definition: A Taylor approximation expresses how a function changes near a specified input using derivatives at that input. The first-order multivariable approximation uses the Jacobian; higher orders include curvature. Approximation accuracy depends on displacement and smoothness. Linearization is therefore local rather than a claim that the underlying robot or network is globally linear. Contact switching can invalidate a smooth local approximation across the switching boundary.
nodes.example: For a pendulum near zero angle, replacing sine of the angle by the angle yields a linear approximation. At larger angles the difference grows. Linearize around the intended operating point and compare the approximation with the original model over the expected state range.
nodes.role_en: Taylor expansions support EKF, LQR, Newton-style optimization and sensitivity analysis of world models. Their validity region should be separated from empirical learned-model generalization. Check the approximation on nearby actual trajectories.

notation.meaning: Jacobian evaluated at the expansion point.

nodes.explain: A Taylor approximation expresses how a function changes near a specified input using derivatives at that input. The first-order multivariable approximation uses the Jacobian; higher orders include curvature. Approximation accuracy depends on displacement and smoothness. Linearization is therefore local rather than a claim that the underlying robot or network is globally linear. Contact switching can invalidate a smooth local approximation across the switching boundary.
nodes.role: Taylor expansions support EKF, LQR, Newton-style optimization and sensitivity analysis of world models. Their validity region should be separated from empirical learned-model generalization. Check the approximation on nearby actual trajectories.

nodes.title: 海森矩阵
nodes.summary: The Hessian collects second partial derivatives of a scalar function.
nodes.definition: The Hessian collects second partial derivatives of a scalar function. It describes local curvature and appears in second-order Taylor approximations and Newton-type optimization. For sufficiently smooth functions it is symmetric. Positive curvature in every nonzero direction helps characterize a strict local minimum, but a Hessian at one point does not establish global convexity. Large neural-network Hessians are often accessed through products rather than explicitly stored.
nodes.example: For a loss equal to the first parameter squared plus three times the second parameter squared, the Hessian is diagonal with entries two and six. The second direction has greater curvature, so an identical coordinate displacement produces a larger quadratic loss increase.
nodes.role_en: Curvature connects optimization conditioning, local trajectory optimization and numerical stability. It is useful background rather than a required explicit matrix in CEM-based ID-WM planning. Use curvature diagnostics with an explicit operating point.
nodes.latex: H_{ij}(x)=\frac{\partial^2 f}{\partial x_i\partial x_j},\qquad f(x+\delta)\approx f(x)+\nabla f(x)^\top\delta+\tfrac12\delta^\top H(x)\delta

nodes.explain: The Hessian collects second partial derivatives of a scalar function. It describes local curvature and appears in second-order Taylor approximations and Newton-type optimization. For sufficiently smooth functions it is symmetric. Positive curvature in every nonzero direction helps characterize a strict local minimum, but a Hessian at one point does not establish global convexity. Large neural-network Hessians are often accessed through products rather than explicitly stored.

nodes.title: 常微分方程
nodes.summary: An ordinary differential equation specifies a time derivative in terms of state, input and time.
nodes.definition: An ordinary differential equation specifies a time derivative in terms of state, input and time. An initial-value problem also supplies a starting state. Solving it produces a trajectory rather than a single scalar. Existence, uniqueness and numerical stability depend on properties of the dynamics. A simulator approximates that solution using finite steps, while a learned discrete transition may approximate the result directly.
nodes.example: A freely moving point with constant velocity satisfies position derivative equal to that velocity. A spring adds a state-dependent acceleration, so position and velocity must be integrated together. Two simulations with different time steps need not produce identical numerical trajectories.
nodes.role_en: ODEs connect physical dynamics to integrators, differentiable simulation and continuous-time flow models. They explain what a discrete learned transition is approximating in many robot environments.

nodes.title: 欧拉与半隐式积分
nodes.summary: Explicit Euler approximates the state derivative at the beginning of a step.
nodes.definition: Explicit Euler approximates the state derivative at the beginning of a step. Semi-implicit Euler updates velocity first and uses the updated velocity for position. Their stability and energy behaviour differ, especially for oscillatory mechanical systems. Smaller steps usually reduce discretization error but increase computational work. Neither integration method removes errors caused by incorrect physical parameters or contact models. The update order is part of the implemented transition function.
nodes.example: For a falling point initially at rest, explicit Euler leaves position unchanged on the first step while updating velocity. Semi-implicit Euler also moves the position using the new downward velocity. Over many steps these conventions produce different trajectories. Choose one convention consistently.
nodes.role_en: Integrator choice and physics substeps affect simulator transitions used to train world models. Policy frequency, physics time step and data sampling interval must be documented separately.

nodes.title: 龙格—库塔积分
nodes.summary: Runge–Kutta methods combine derivative evaluations at intermediate states to approximate an ODE solution.
nodes.definition: Runge–Kutta methods combine derivative evaluations at intermediate states to approximate an ODE solution. Classical RK4 has fourth-order global accuracy for sufficiently smooth problems under standard assumptions, but it uses four derivative evaluations per step. Error order does not by itself establish stability for a stiff system. Discontinuous impacts require appropriate event or contact treatment rather than assuming a high-order smooth integrator resolves them automatically.
nodes.example: Integrate a smooth pendulum trajectory with Euler and RK4 over the same interval. Compare error against a much finer reference solution and report both derivative evaluations and wall-clock time. At a contact event, examine whether the simulator changes modes inside the step.
nodes.role_en: Higher-order integration explains simulation accuracy–cost tradeoffs and ODE-based generative sampling. It does not imply every robot training pipeline should choose RK4. Compare numerical error and wall-clock cost together.

nodes.title: 奇异值分解
nodes.summary: Singular value decomposition expresses a matrix as orthogonal input and output directions together with nonnegative scale factors.
nodes.definition: Singular value decomposition expresses a matrix as orthogonal input and output directions together with nonnegative scale factors. It exists for rectangular matrices and separates rank, dominant directions and near-singular directions. Small singular values indicate directions that are weakly mapped and can amplify errors in inversion. Truncation can provide a low-rank approximation, but the retained rank must fit the application and noise level.
nodes.example: A robot Jacobian near a singular configuration has a small singular value. Requesting end-effector motion along the corresponding weak direction can require very large joint velocities if the matrix is inverted without regularization. Plotting singular values exposes that numerical issue.
nodes.role_en: SVD supports pseudoinverses, damped inverse kinematics, PCA and conditioning diagnostics. It links linear algebra to geometric robot control and feature compression. Check singular values before commanding joint velocities.

notation.meaning: Diagonal or rectangular diagonal matrix of nonnegative singular values.

nodes.title: 伪逆与阻尼最小二乘
nodes.summary: A pseudoinverse generalizes matrix inversion to rectangular or rank-deficient systems.
nodes.definition: A pseudoinverse generalizes matrix inversion to rectangular or rank-deficient systems. It can select a least-squares solution and, under the standard criterion, a minimum-norm solution among alternatives. Damped least squares replaces unstable inversion of very small singular values with a regularized compromise. Damping changes the requested motion and does not guarantee joint-limit or collision avoidance. Those requirements need additional constraints or objectives.
nodes.example: A seven-joint arm may have many joint increments producing the same small hand displacement. A pseudoinverse selects one according to its norm criterion. Near a singularity, damping prevents an arbitrarily large joint command at the cost of residual task error.
nodes.role_en: This is a key link from Jacobians to inverse kinematics and local control. Compare its assumptions with learned inverse planning rather than equating the two algorithms.

nodes.en: Positive Definite Matrices and Quadratic Forms
nodes.title: 正定矩阵与二次型
nodes.summary: A symmetric positive semidefinite matrix gives a nonnegative quadratic form.
nodes.definition: A symmetric positive semidefinite matrix gives a nonnegative quadratic form. Positive definite matrices give strictly positive values for all nonzero vectors. These properties determine whether weighted error costs can become negative and whether certain covariance or optimization operations are well defined. A covariance may be semidefinite rather than invertible. Numerical symmetry and small negative eigenvalues can reveal computation or modelling problems.
nodes.example: Weight a planar position error using a diagonal matrix with entries one and four. An equal numerical error in the second coordinate contributes four times as much cost. Setting one weight to zero ignores that direction and makes the quadratic form semidefinite.
nodes.role_en: Quadratic costs, covariance matrices, LQR weights and Lyapunov candidates all use these concepts. The mathematical conditions should be checked rather than inferred from a matrix name.

notation.meaning: Strictly positive quadratic form for every nonzero vector.

nodes.title: 约束优化与KKT条件
nodes.summary: Constrained optimization selects a decision while respecting equality and inequality restrictions.
nodes.definition: Constrained optimization selects a decision while respecting equality and inequality restrictions. Under suitable constraint qualifications, KKT conditions combine stationarity, feasibility, multiplier nonnegativity and complementary slackness at a local solution. They are not an unrestricted global-optimality certificate for nonconvex problems. Robot trajectory constraints include dynamics, actuator bounds, joint limits and collision distances; penalties approximate some restrictions but are not automatically equivalent to hard constraints.
nodes.example: Minimize joint motion subject to reaching a hand target and staying within joint limits. A joint limit can become active, meaning the solution lies exactly on the boundary. A soft penalty may permit a violation if reducing another cost is sufficiently attractive.
nodes.role_en: This node supports trajectory optimization, contact formulations and constrained control. It helps distinguish ID-WM regularization from formally enforced physical feasibility. Solver feasibility and execution feasibility require separate checks.

nodes.title: 旋转矩阵与SO(3)
nodes.summary: SO(3) is the set of proper three-dimensional rotation matrices.
nodes.definition: SO(3) is the set of proper three-dimensional rotation matrices. Orthogonality preserves vector lengths and angles, while determinant one excludes reflections. Rotations can express orientations, transform coordinate representations or actively rotate vectors; those uses require consistent conventions. Composition generally depends on order. A matrix with nine free entries is not automatically a valid rotation, so optimization and learning must handle its constraints.
nodes.example: Rotate a vector by ninety degrees around the z-axis, then around the x-axis. Reversing the order generally gives a different result. If a learned matrix slowly loses orthogonality, it can distort lengths even though it is labelled a rotation. Check the rotation convention.
nodes.role_en: Rotation representations enter robot state construction, camera extrinsics, pose estimation and dynamics. They are a geometric prerequisite rather than a distinct kind of neural network.

nodes.title: 刚体变换与SE(3)
nodes.summary: SE(3) combines a rotation with a translation using homogeneous coordinates.
nodes.definition: SE(3) combines a rotation with a translation using homogeneous coordinates. Multiplication composes frame transformations, and inversion reverses their direction. The notation must specify source and target frames; otherwise the same numerical matrix can be used incorrectly. A pose is a geometric configuration, while a twist describes its instantaneous motion. Their dimensions and transformation rules differ, even when both appear in a robot state vector.
nodes.example: Compose a world-to-base transform with a base-to-camera transform to locate the camera in the world. Reversing the product or using a camera-to-base matrix without inversion produces a different pose, often causing projected points to appear behind the camera. Write frame labels explicitly.
nodes.role_en: Rigid transforms connect forward kinematics, camera calibration, SLAM and world-model state representations. Correct frame semantics are essential before learned-model errors can be interpreted. Keep source and target frames explicit.

notation.meaning: Orientation and position of one frame relative to another.

nodes.title: 单位四元数
nodes.summary: A unit quaternion is a four-coordinate representation of a three-dimensional rotation.
nodes.definition: A unit quaternion is a four-coordinate representation of a three-dimensional rotation. Its unit-norm constraint and double-cover property require care in losses and interpolation. Quaternion component ordering varies across APIs, commonly scalar-first or scalar-last. Normalization alone does not establish a consistent sign sequence or coordinate-frame convention. Orientation differences should use a rotation-aware metric rather than unrestricted Euclidean subtraction of four components.
nodes.example: The quaternions with all signs reversed represent the same physical orientation. A direct squared component loss can report a large error between them. Before comparing recorded and predicted orientations, check ordering, normalization, sign equivalence and whether the pose is expressed in world or body coordinates.
nodes.role_en: Quaternions are common in humanoid datasets and simulator state interfaces. Their conventions must match across data generation, policy input and evaluation. Audit the serialized data format before training.

nodes.en: Angular Velocity, Twists and the Adjoint
nodes.title: 角速度、旋量与伴随变换
nodes.summary: A twist combines angular and linear velocity for rigid-body motion.
nodes.definition: A twist combines angular and linear velocity for rigid-body motion. Its coordinates depend on the chosen frame and reference point. The adjoint transformation converts between space and body representations under a consistent convention. The linear component is not always the velocity of whichever point is informally called the origin. Explicitly identifying ordering and frame prevents incorrect Jacobian, force and controller calculations.
nodes.example: A rotating rigid body gives different point velocities at its centre and at a distant attached point. Translating the reference point therefore changes the linear twist component even when angular velocity is unchanged. The adjoint accounts for that coupling. Keep the reference point explicit.
nodes.role_en: Twists connect geometric pose representations to robot Jacobians, operational-space control and rigid-body dynamics. Learned velocity states must preserve these same frame conventions. State ordering must match each consuming API.

notation.meaning: Angular and linear components under a stated twist convention.

nodes.title: 刚体运动的指数坐标
nodes.summary: Exponential coordinates represent finite rigid motion through an underlying infinitesimal generator.
nodes.definition: Exponential coordinates represent finite rigid motion through an underlying infinitesimal generator. For a constant screw axis, the matrix exponential produces a rigid transformation. This formulation provides a compact way to compose joint motions and perform local pose updates on a group. The exponential and logarithm maps have conventions and local ambiguities; they are not ordinary elementwise exponentials or logarithms of matrix entries.
nodes.example: A revolute joint rotates an attached link around its fixed axis. Exponentiating the joint screw axis times its angle yields the corresponding transform. Multiplying joint exponentials in chain order produces the end-effector pose relative to the reference configuration. The multiplication order is essential.
nodes.role_en: The product-of-exponentials formulation supports forward kinematics, pose residuals and Lie-group state estimation. It connects calculus, matrix algebra and geometry. Use the same motion convention across every joint.

notation.meaning: Screw axis represented as a twist.
Matrix representation of the twist generator.

nodes.title: 物理量、单位与量纲
nodes.summary: Dimensional analysis checks whether terms in a physical equation have compatible units.
nodes.definition: Dimensional analysis checks whether terms in a physical equation have compatible units. Numerical values alone do not specify a physical quantity: metres and centimetres, radians and degrees, and seconds and simulation steps require conversion. Normalized machine-learning features hide units but do not remove their physical meanings. A physically meaningful loss may require scaling heterogeneous state components before combining them. Units remain relevant after numerical normalization.
nodes.example: A velocity of one metre per second integrated over twenty milliseconds changes position by two centimetres. Treating the number twenty as seconds produces a thousandfold error. Similarly, a force limit is not interchangeable with a torque limit unless a lever arm is specified.
nodes.role_en: Unit audits are basic checks for simulator assets, dynamics labels, state normalization and controller commands. They often explain apparent model failures before architecture changes are needed.

nodes.title: 牛顿平动动力学
nodes.summary: Newtonian translation dynamics relates total external force to the acceleration of a constant-mass body in an inertial frame.
nodes.definition: Newtonian translation dynamics relates total external force to the acceleration of a constant-mass body in an inertial frame. Momentum expresses the combined role of mass and velocity. Gravity, contact and actuator forces must be assembled in a consistent frame. Internal forces can cancel in whole-system momentum while still changing internal configuration. This simple relation is a building block rather than a complete articulated-robot model.
nodes.example: A two-kilogram object acted on by a net horizontal force of four newtons accelerates at two metres per second squared. If friction also acts, subtract its force before applying the relation; a commanded motor value is not automatically the net force on the object.
nodes.role_en: These mechanics underpin simulator transitions, contact reasoning and learned dynamics interpretation. They motivate why known state, physical parameters and action meaning all matter. The net-force definition must remain explicit.

notation.meaning: Constant mass in the stated model.

nodes.title: 力矩与角动量
nodes.summary: Torque describes how a force applied away from a reference point tends to change angular momentum.
nodes.definition: Torque describes how a force applied away from a reference point tends to change angular momentum. The reference point and coordinate frame must be specified. Force magnitude alone is insufficient: direction and lever arm determine rotational effect. For a general rigid body, angular momentum need not be parallel to angular velocity. Joint torque commands act through the robot mechanism and do not directly specify arbitrary Cartesian forces.
nodes.example: The same ten-newton perpendicular force applied at a lever arm of one tenth of a metre produces one newton-metre of torque; doubling the perpendicular lever arm doubles the torque. A force directed along the lever arm produces no torque about that point.
nodes.role_en: Torque and momentum connect actuator limits, rigid-body inertia, inverse dynamics and contact forces. They clarify the physical meaning of actions used to collect world-model training transitions.

notation.meaning: Lever-arm vector from the reference point to force application.

nodes.title: 质量分布与惯性张量
nodes.summary: The inertia tensor summarizes how a rigid body mass distribution resists rotational acceleration about a specified point.
nodes.definition: The inertia tensor summarizes how a rigid body mass distribution resists rotational acceleration about a specified point. Its entries depend on reference frame and origin. It also defines rotational kinetic energy. A total mass does not uniquely determine inertia. Imported robot assets can therefore have plausible visual geometry but incorrect dynamic behaviour if centre of mass or inertia is wrong. Physical consistency imposes constraints beyond merely having positive diagonal entries.
nodes.example: Two bodies can have equal mass while one places more mass farther from the rotation axis. The latter has greater moment of inertia about that axis and needs more torque for the same angular acceleration. Changing the tensor frame without rotating its components is an asset error.
nodes.role_en: Inertia is required for physically meaningful robot simulation and inverse dynamics. Parameter randomization should remain physically coherent rather than independently perturbing arbitrary tensor entries. Validate the asset before collecting training transitions.

notation.meaning: Inertia tensor about a specified point and frame.

nodes.en: Work, Kinetic Energy and Potential Energy
nodes.title: 功、动能与势能
nodes.summary: Work transfers energy through force applied along displacement.
nodes.definition: Work transfers energy through force applied along displacement. Kinetic energy depends on motion, while potential energy depends on configuration and the modeled force field. In conservative ideal mechanics their sum can be preserved; actuators, damping and contact losses alter that balance. Numerical integration can also introduce energy error. A learned dynamics model can fit short transitions while violating long-horizon energy behaviour.
nodes.example: Lifting a one-kilogram mass by one metre near Earth increases gravitational potential energy by approximately 9.81 joules. Sliding friction dissipates mechanical energy. An undamped simulated pendulum whose amplitude steadily increases may reveal integration or modelling error rather than a real energy source.
nodes.role_en: Energy helps derive robot equations, diagnose simulation drift and construct physically informed objectives. Conservation is conditional on the modeled system and must not be assumed during actuated or dissipative motion.

notation.meaning: Work, kinetic energy and gravitational potential energy.
Height relative to a chosen potential reference.

nodes.title: 拉格朗日量与欧拉—拉格朗日方程
nodes.summary: Lagrangian mechanics derives equations of motion using generalized coordinates and energy expressions.
nodes.definition: Lagrangian mechanics derives equations of motion using generalized coordinates and energy expressions. Euler–Lagrange equations combine derivatives with respect to coordinates, velocities and time. Generalized nonconservative forces account for actuation and dissipation not represented by the potential. Constraints require compatible coordinate choices or additional multipliers. The symbol L here means Lagrangian and must be distinguished from a neural-network training loss. Each derivative has a distinct mathematical role.
nodes.example: For a pendulum, rotational kinetic energy and gravitational potential energy produce a nonlinear equation involving angular acceleration and sine of angle. Adding a motor torque places a generalized input on the right-hand side; adding damping requires a dissipative torque term.
nodes.role_en: This derivation explains the mass, velocity-dependent and gravity terms used in articulated robot dynamics. It is a physical foundation for analytical models and simulation-generated learning data.

nodes.title: 机器人广义动力学方程
nodes.summary: The manipulator equation describes coupled articulated-body acceleration under actuator and contact forces.
nodes.definition: The manipulator equation describes coupled articulated-body acceleration under actuator and contact forces. The mass matrix depends on configuration, and velocity-dependent terms account for effects such as Coriolis and centrifugal coupling. A floating-base humanoid can have unactuated coordinates, represented by the input map. Different texts group velocity terms differently, so notation must be matched before comparing formulas. Contact adds force variables and often mode changes.
nodes.example: Moving an arm joint can accelerate other links because the mass matrix couples coordinates. A humanoid joint torque cannot directly command every floating-base acceleration; feet-ground contact and momentum transfer mediate the whole-body response. Verify support contacts and actuator limits when evaluating the requested acceleration.
nodes.role_en: This equation connects classical dynamics, inverse dynamics, model-based control and learned transition models. A neural world model may approximate its discrete consequences without explicitly recovering every physical term.

notation.meaning: Mass matrix, velocity-dependent terms and gravity terms.

nodes.role: This equation connects classical dynamics, inverse dynamics, model-based control and learned transition models. A neural world model may approximate its discrete consequences without explicitly recovering every physical term.

nodes.title: 完整约束与接触冲量
nodes.summary: A holonomic constraint restricts configuration through an equation, and differentiating it produces a velocity restriction.
nodes.definition: A holonomic constraint restricts configuration through an equation, and differentiating it produces a velocity restriction. Constraint forces enforce the restriction rather than acting as arbitrary independent commands. Impacts can produce discontinuous velocity changes represented by impulses. Continuous accelerations and instantaneous impulses require different numerical handling. Contact events make a robot a hybrid system whose active constraints change with configuration and interaction.
nodes.example: An ideal foot fixed to the ground has zero contact-point velocity during stance. At touchdown, the predicted pre-impact velocity may change abruptly through a contact impulse. Integrating a smooth unconstrained model through that instant can incorrectly predict penetration or continued free motion.
nodes.role_en: Constraint and impact concepts explain difficult regions for learned dynamics, differentiable simulation and locomotion transfer. Smooth training losses do not remove the underlying contact-mode changes.

notation.meaning: Impulse integrated over an impact event.

nodes.title: 库仑摩擦与接触可行性
nodes.summary: Coulomb friction limits tangential contact force relative to normal force.
nodes.definition: Coulomb friction limits tangential contact force relative to normal force. Sticking and sliding follow different conditions, and numerical simulators may use regularized or approximate friction models. A friction coefficient alone does not specify all contact behaviour; compliance, solver settings, geometry and restitution can also matter. Contact feasibility restricts which commanded accelerations or forces can be physically realized without slipping or losing support.
nodes.example: A robot foot can slip if the required tangential force exceeds the available friction bound. Increasing the policy reward for speed does not increase that physical bound. Comparing simulation and hardware requires checking contact materials and the actual normal-force distribution.
nodes.role_en: Friction is central to whole-body control, ball contact and sim-to-real transfer. Randomization can improve robustness only over the conditions represented and actually tested. Inspect both sticking and sliding failure cases.

nodes.title: 正向运动学
nodes.summary: Forward kinematics maps joint configuration to the pose of an end effector or other link.
nodes.definition: Forward kinematics maps joint configuration to the pose of an end effector or other link. It uses robot geometry and joint conventions, without requiring forces or accelerations. Multiple configurations can produce the same task-space pose. Frame attachment, joint offsets and ordering are part of the model. A correct joint vector can produce an incorrect reported pose if the kinematic tree or reference frames are wrong.
nodes.example: For a planar two-link arm, the hand position depends on both link lengths and the sum of joint rotations along the chain. Changing a link length changes the predicted hand location even if the recorded joint angles remain unchanged. Check the reference pose too.
nodes.role_en: Forward kinematics validates retargeted robot data, computes task-space rewards and supplies geometric features. Kinematic agreement does not by itself demonstrate dynamic balance or successful contact execution.

nodes.title: 机器人雅可比与微分运动学
nodes.summary: The robot Jacobian maps joint velocities to an instantaneous end-effector twist.
nodes.definition: The robot Jacobian maps joint velocities to an instantaneous end-effector twist. It depends on configuration and coordinate conventions. Rank loss identifies task directions that cannot be produced instantaneously. A geometric Jacobian and an analytical Jacobian of orientation parameters are related but not automatically identical. Differential kinematics is local; integrating a large joint increment using a single Jacobian can introduce substantial geometric error.
nodes.example: At a stretched planar arm configuration, some hand-motion directions require very large joint velocities or cannot be produced instantaneously. Computing singular values of the Jacobian quantifies the loss of local control authority. Small requested displacements must still be verified by recomputing forward kinematics.
nodes.role_en: Jacobians connect forward geometry to inverse kinematics, Cartesian control, contact forces and sensitivity. They also provide analytical checks for learned kinematic or dynamics gradients. Local predictions require geometric execution checks.

nodes.title: 逆运动学
nodes.summary: Inverse kinematics finds joint configurations that realize a desired task-space pose.
nodes.definition: Inverse kinematics finds joint configurations that realize a desired task-space pose. Numerical methods repeatedly compute a pose error and update joints using a local Jacobian. Solutions may be multiple, absent or constrained by joint limits and obstacles. Orientation errors require a compatible geometric representation. Reaching a pose kinematically does not prove that a torque-controlled robot can execute it dynamically or maintain balance.
nodes.example: A redundant arm can reach one hand position with different elbow placements. An unconstrained numerical solver may choose a configuration near a joint limit. Adding a null-space objective or explicit constraints changes the solution criterion rather than merely improving numerical accuracy.
nodes.role_en: IK supports retargeting, task-space command generation and motion initialization. It is distinct from ID-WM inverse planning, which searches actions through a learned forward transition model.

nodes.title: 逆动力学与计算力矩控制
nodes.summary: Inverse dynamics computes forces or torques required for a specified motion under a physical model.
nodes.definition: Inverse dynamics computes forces or torques required for a specified motion under a physical model. Computed-torque control combines model compensation with feedback to track a trajectory. The displayed expression omits contacts and underactuation for clarity. Real robots require actuator limits, state estimation and contact feasibility. Errors in mass, friction, delay or unmodelled forces can make the computed torque insufficient or inaccurate.
nodes.example: A joint moving upward against gravity needs torque even when its desired angular acceleration is zero. A gravity-compensating model supplies that contribution; feedback then corrects tracking error. Merely replaying desired joint positions does not perform inverse dynamics. Check actuator saturation separately.
nodes.role_en: This provides a classical alternative and physical reference for learned control. It helps separate force prediction, position targets and the learned forward dynamics used for differentiable policy training.

nodes.title: 比例—微分控制
nodes.summary: PD control applies a correction based on position error and velocity error.
nodes.definition: PD control applies a correction based on position error and velocity error. Gains determine response speed, damping and sensitivity, while actuator saturation and measurement noise affect practical performance. The formula does not alone guarantee stability for every nonlinear robot, delay or contact regime. In many robot-learning systems, a policy outputs desired positions that are converted into torques by a lower-level PD controller.
nodes.example: A policy output of 0.1 radians can mean a desired joint offset, not a torque. The actual torque depends on current position, velocity, gains and clipping. Two simulators using the same policy checkpoint can therefore move differently if their PD settings differ.
nodes.role_en: PD control is essential context for humanoid policy action semantics and sim-to-real matching. Record gains, control frequency, decimation and effort limits alongside neural architecture. These parameters belong in reproducible experiment configurations.

nodes.title: 比例—积分—微分控制
nodes.summary: PID control adds integral action to proportional and derivative feedback.
nodes.definition: PID control adds integral action to proportional and derivative feedback. Accumulated error can remove certain steady-state offsets, but actuator saturation may cause integrator windup. Derivative measurements require filtering or careful state estimation. The controller needs a discrete implementation and timing convention on a computer. Tuning gains for one system does not establish robustness for a changed load, delay or contact condition.
nodes.example: A velocity controller with a constant unmodelled resistance may settle below the requested speed under proportional control. Integral action increases the command while an error persists. If the motor saturates, anti-windup logic prevents unlimited accumulation that would delay recovery. Log the accumulated error.
nodes.role_en: PID links calculus to practical robot and actuator loops. It is a classical control background component, not a prerequisite for every learned world-model planner. Its timing convention affects the discrete implementation.

nodes.title: 线性状态空间系统
nodes.summary: A linear state-space model represents coupled state evolution and measurement with matrices.
nodes.definition: A linear state-space model represents coupled state evolution and measurement with matrices. It can describe an exactly linear system or a local approximation around an operating point. The state dimension differs from the number of sensors or controls. Continuous- and discrete-time matrices are not interchangeable. Such models make concepts including controllability, observability, feedback eigenvalues and Kalman filtering mathematically explicit. The operating point and sampling convention must be stated.
nodes.example: A point mass with position and velocity has a two-dimensional state even if only position is measured. Force is one control input. The model shows why velocity can matter for prediction despite not being directly observed at a single instant.
nodes.role_en: State-space systems connect physical dynamics to LQR and state estimation. They are interpretable baselines and local approximations alongside neural world models. Keep continuous and discrete representations separate.
