nodes.summary: Trajectory linearization differentiates nonlinear dynamics around a nominal state-input trajectory.
nodes.definition: Trajectory linearization differentiates nonlinear dynamics around a nominal state-input trajectory. The resulting matrices can change with time. It describes local perturbations rather than replacing the complete nonlinear system. A valid nominal trajectory should itself satisfy dynamics, or an additional defect term must be retained. Crossing a contact-mode boundary requires appropriate hybrid treatment rather than applying an unchanged smooth linear approximation.
nodes.example: Linearizing an upright pendulum and a downward pendulum produces different local behaviour. A controller designed for one equilibrium is not automatically valid near the other. Compare the linear approximation with nearby nonlinear rollouts before using it for control. Its validity is local.
nodes.role_en: Linearization supports time-varying LQR, EKF, trajectory optimization and learned-model sensitivity analysis. Its local assumptions complement but do not replace empirical rollout validation. Test perturbations within the intended operating region.

nodes.summary: Controllability asks whether inputs can move a state through the required directions in a specified model.
nodes.definition: Controllability asks whether inputs can move a state through the required directions in a specified model. Observability asks whether state can be inferred from outputs over time. Rank tests characterize these properties for finite-dimensional linear time-invariant systems. They do not directly prove global nonlinear reachability or sensor adequacy in all environments. An underactuated system may still be controllable through dynamic coupling.
nodes.example: A position measurement over several times can reveal velocity for a moving point, although one position sample cannot. Conversely, an unmeasured coordinate with no effect on any future output remains unobservable in the model. State inference requires an observation history rather than one image alone.
nodes.role_en: These concepts clarify action authority and hidden-state estimation. They help assess whether a world-model input or controller can support the intended robot task at all.

nodes.summary: LQR computes optimal linear feedback for linear dynamics and a quadratic objective under specified assumptions.
nodes.definition: LQR computes optimal linear feedback for linear dynamics and a quadratic objective under specified assumptions. The Riccati equation determines the gain, with stabilizability and detectability conditions relevant to the infinite-horizon result. The controller balances state error against control effort. Applying LQR to a nonlinear robot typically means stabilizing a local model or tracking a nominal trajectory, not obtaining globally optimal robot behaviour.
nodes.example: A cart position regulator can penalize large position error and large motor force. Increasing the force penalty generally reduces aggressive control. For a nonlinear pendulum, an upright LQR controller usually needs an appropriate initial region or a separate swing-up strategy.
nodes.role_en: LQR is a fundamental classical comparison for model-based control, and its local reasoning supports modern trajectory optimization. It is not equivalent to CEM or a learned policy.

nodes.title: 李雅普诺夫稳定性
nodes.summary: Lyapunov analysis studies stability through a scalar function with suitable positivity and derivative properties.
nodes.definition: Lyapunov analysis studies stability through a scalar function with suitable positivity and derivative properties. Nonincrease can establish stability under appropriate assumptions; asymptotic convergence generally requires stronger conditions or an invariance argument. The region where conditions hold matters. A plotted decreasing training loss is not a Lyapunov certificate for a physical robot, because the loss and closed-loop state evolution are different objects.
nodes.example: For a damped linear oscillator, an energy-like function can decrease along trajectories. If that derivative condition is verified only near an equilibrium, the conclusion is local. A neural controller that succeeds on sampled rollouts has empirical evidence, not automatically a formal stability proof.
nodes.role_en: This node distinguishes theoretical closed-loop guarantees from training objectives and task success rates. It is relevant to safe control and model-error reasoning around learned robot policies.

nodes.title: 轨迹优化
nodes.summary: Trajectory optimization jointly or implicitly chooses a finite state-input sequence to minimize cost while respecting dynamics and other constraints.
nodes.definition: Trajectory optimization jointly or implicitly chooses a finite state-input sequence to minimize cost while respecting dynamics and other constraints. Direct shooting optimizes controls through rollouts; direct transcription also includes states as decision variables. Nonlinear problems can have local minima and infeasible initializations. The quality of a computed solution depends on the model, discretization, solver tolerances and whether execution follows the predicted trajectory.
nodes.example: Plan an arm reach that avoids an obstacle while limiting joint torque. A kinematically smooth path can still be dynamically infeasible. Check the optimized trajectory by replaying it through the simulator with the actual controller and reporting constraint violations. Report the execution discrepancy.
nodes.role_en: Trajectory optimization links classical control with model-based learning. MPC repeatedly solves finite-horizon versions, while ID-WM uses a different hierarchical model and CEM search organization. Validate the returned motion through execution.

nodes.title: 碰撞几何与构型空间
nodes.summary: Configuration space represents the robot using generalized coordinates.
nodes.definition: Configuration space represents the robot using generalized coordinates. Collision checking maps a configuration to occupied link geometry and tests it against obstacles or other links. Workspace clearance for an end-effector alone does not establish whole-robot clearance. Discrete collision checks can miss collisions between sampled configurations, so interpolation, swept-volume reasoning or sufficiently conservative checking is required for reliable planning. Collision margins should be specified explicitly.
nodes.example: An arm hand can avoid a table while its elbow intersects the table edge. Evaluating only the hand point would incorrectly declare the motion safe. A joint interpolation between two collision-free endpoints can also collide in the middle. Check intermediate states too.
nodes.role_en: Collision geometry is essential for robot planning and simulation. It explains why a small latent-space distance or plausible generated image is not a collision-avoidance guarantee.

notation.meaning: Robot occupied geometry at configuration q.
Signed or separation distance under the stated convention.

nodes.title: 基于采样的运动规划
nodes.summary: Sampling-based planners such as PRM and RRT construct connectivity using sampled configurations and local collision-checked motions.
nodes.definition: Sampling-based planners such as PRM and RRT construct connectivity using sampled configurations and local collision-checked motions. Their guarantees depend on algorithm assumptions, sampling and connection procedures; finite-time success is not guaranteed. Geometric planning can ignore dynamics, while kinodynamic variants incorporate them. A learned state generator can be compared by what it samples and how local transitions are validated, without calling it the same algorithm.
nodes.example: Build a search tree for an arm by sampling joint configurations, extending from nearby nodes and rejecting colliding connections. A narrow passage can require many samples. Increasing samples improves coverage possibilities but does not remove errors in collision geometry or the local steering routine.
nodes.role_en: These classical methods provide context for reachability, hierarchical subgoals and model-based planning. They connect explicit geometry to the local-future composition used by learned planners. Check every connection using the actual robot model.

nodes.title: 递归贝叶斯状态估计
nodes.summary: Recursive Bayesian estimation maintains a probability distribution over hidden state.
nodes.definition: Recursive Bayesian estimation maintains a probability distribution over hidden state. A prediction step propagates the previous belief through dynamics, and a measurement update combines it with the current likelihood. The belief need not be Gaussian; different filters approximate it differently. A point prediction does not by itself represent uncertainty. Correct time alignment and measurement models are as important as the choice of filtering algorithm.
nodes.example: A ball detector provides a noisy image position while a dynamics model predicts motion. The filter first predicts where the ball may be, then uses the new measurement to update that belief. During missed detections it can continue prediction, with uncertainty generally growing.
nodes.role_en: State estimation supplies the current state or belief used by controllers and world models. It addresses partial observation rather than replacing planning or task-policy learning.

nodes.title: 卡尔曼滤波
nodes.summary: The Kalman filter gives exact recursive Gaussian state estimation for the specified linear Gaussian model.
nodes.definition: The Kalman filter gives exact recursive Gaussian state estimation for the specified linear Gaussian model. It propagates mean and covariance, then weights measurement residuals using predicted uncertainty and measurement noise. Correctness is relative to those model assumptions, not all physical systems. Numerical implementations must maintain covariance consistency and handle initialization, outliers and missing measurements. A gain is determined by uncertainty rather than an arbitrary trust percentage.
nodes.example: If a position sensor is very noisy, increasing its measurement covariance reduces how much the update changes the predicted position. A more precise measurement usually receives greater weight, provided the process and measurement models are correctly calibrated. Measurement confidence must be calibrated.
nodes.role_en: Kalman filtering is useful for robot and ball-state estimates that feed control or planning. It offers a classical uncertainty-aware baseline for learned state estimation. Report initialization and missing-measurement handling too.

It is generally approximate and can become inconsistent when nonlinearities, initialization errors or unmodelled effects are severe. Jacobians must match coordinate representations; rotations often require an error-state or manifold-aware formulation. Covariance propagation should not be interpreted as an exact uncertainty bound outside the approximation assumptions.
nodes.example: A camera observes a 3D point through perspective division. The measurement is nonlinear in position, so an EKF uses a projection Jacobian around the current estimate. A point near the camera plane or a badly initialized depth can make that approximation unreliable.
nodes.role_en: EKF connects calculus and geometry to sensor fusion, localization and world-model state input. Learned transition Jacobians can be used, but their accuracy and uncertainty must be validated.

nodes.title: 传感器模型与时间同步融合
nodes.summary: Sensor fusion combines measurements using explicit models of what each sensor measures, where it is mounted and when it was captured.
nodes.definition: Sensor fusion combines measurements using explicit models of what each sensor measures, where it is mounted and when it was captured. Different sensors can have distinct rates, delays, coordinate frames and noise. Combining values with matching array shapes does not ensure physical consistency. Correlated errors require care because treating them as independent can make estimated uncertainty too small. Calibration and synchronization are part of the model.
nodes.example: A camera image delayed by fifty milliseconds should not be combined as if it measured the current position of a fast-moving ball. Propagate the relevant state to the image timestamp or use a suitable delayed-update method before fusing it with current joint and inertial data.

Identifiability asks whether the available experiment can distinguish parameter values; low prediction error alone does not ensure physically correct recovered parameters. Data collection must excite relevant modes, and validation should use trajectories beyond those used for fitting. Noise and hidden state can bias results.
nodes.example: If every recorded joint motion is nearly static, inertial parameters may be poorly identified even though gravity behaviour is fitted well. Faster varied excitation can reveal effects absent from the original data, subject to the physical limits of the robot.
nodes.role_en: System identification bridges analytical models, simulators and learned world models. It supports calibration and explains why more data of an uninformative type may not resolve a dynamics ambiguity.

Successful import only shows that a description was accepted; it does not validate joint conventions, inertia, contacts or actuator behaviour. Visual meshes may be unsuitable collision geometry, and missing data can be replaced by defaults that alter dynamics.

nodes.summary: MuJoCo is a general-purpose physics engine for articulated structures interacting with their environment.
nodes.definition: MuJoCo is a general-purpose physics engine for articulated structures interacting with their environment. Its model, state and numerical settings jointly define transitions. Contact uses engine-specific modelling and solver choices rather than a universally exact physical law. Rendering, dynamics computation and control interfaces are different subsystems. Version and configuration must be recorded when using it to produce trajectories, evaluate policies or compare learned dynamics.
nodes.example: A policy can output joint position targets that MuJoCo actuators convert into forces. Changing actuator gains, contact parameters or integration time step changes transitions even with the same policy weights. A rendered successful pose is not the same as stable closed-loop execution.
nodes.role_en: MuJoCo provides a conventional simulator baseline and data source for robot world models. A learned differentiable surrogate can be trained from its transitions without differentiating the simulator itself.

nodes.definition: MJX is MuJoCo ecosystem support for accelerator-oriented simulation and JAX-compatible workflows. Its available implementations, supported features and performance properties depend on version and backend. Batched array computation and compilation can make many environments efficient, but compilation cost, contact workloads and memory use matter. A simulator running on accelerators is not automatically differentiable through every operation, nor numerically identical to another backend.
nodes.example: Compile a batched step function, then time warmed-up repeated steps separately from compilation. Check that the selected robot features and contact settings are supported. Compare corresponding short trajectories before interpreting a speed difference as an equal-fidelity simulation improvement. Exclude compilation from steady-state timing.

Differentiability depends on actual operations, state updates and contact treatment. Efficient parallel execution, gradient availability and physical-model fidelity should be evaluated separately. Backend-specific numerical settings remain important.
nodes.example: A batch of independent robot states can be advanced by GPU kernels. A Warp tape can differentiate supported computations of a scalar loss, but this does not establish that arbitrary simulator contact rollouts expose reliable derivatives. Consult the backend feature and differentiation documentation.
nodes.role_en: Warp connects the numerical-kernel layer to physics workloads and large-batch robot learning. It should not be conflated with a learned differentiable world model or with video rendering.

nodes.summary: Differentiable simulation exposes derivatives of simulated outcomes with respect to inputs or parameters.
nodes.definition: Differentiable simulation exposes derivatives of simulated outcomes with respect to inputs or parameters. It may use automatic, analytical, implicit or approximate differentiation. The resulting derivative belongs to the implemented numerical model, which may regularize physical discontinuities. Gradient existence, numerical stability and usefulness for optimization are different properties. Contact-mode changes and long horizons can make derivatives difficult even when a software framework supports backward execution.
nodes.example: Optimize an applied force so a simulated point reaches a target. A smooth free-flight trajectory gives straightforward sensitivities. If the point collides or changes friction mode, compare analytic gradients with finite differences away from and near the switching boundary. Compare several perturbation sizes.
nodes.role_en: This branch explains differentiable physics and learned differentiable surrogates. SuperMimic can differentiate its learned world model without differentiating the rigid-body simulator used to collect transitions.

nodes.title: 域随机化
nodes.summary: Domain randomization varies selected environment parameters during training to encourage robustness over a distribution of conditions.
nodes.definition: Domain randomization varies selected environment parameters during training to encourage robustness over a distribution of conditions. Parameters can include mass, friction, actuator response, delay, sensor noise and appearance. Randomization must respect physical consistency and task relevance. Broader variation is not automatically better: it can slow learning or include impossible combinations. Robustness outside the sampled and evaluated distribution remains an empirical question.
nodes.example: Vary foot friction and actuator strength across simulated environments, then test the resulting policy on held-out combinations. Randomizing only colour does not cover changes in contact dynamics, while randomizing mass without updating compatible inertia may create inconsistent assets. Inspect randomized assets before training.
nodes.role_en: Domain randomization connects uncertainty modelling to policy transfer and robust world-model data. Report ranges, correlations and deployment tests rather than claiming guaranteed sim-to-real success. Validate the intended deployment conditions directly.

nodes.title: 仿真到现实迁移与验证
nodes.summary: Sim-to-real transfer deploys a model or controller trained using simulation into a physical system.
nodes.definition: Sim-to-real transfer deploys a model or controller trained using simulation into a physical system. Mismatch can arise in dynamics, contact, actuators, delays, observations and task conditions. Asset checks, simulation validation and hardware trials establish different evidence levels. Adaptation or randomization can address some gaps but does not replace physical evaluation. Safe operating limits and concrete task acceptance criteria should be defined for the actual robot experiment.
nodes.example: A simulated humanoid policy may transfer basic walking yet fail precise ball placement because foot-ball contact and sensing were not covered. Evaluate balance, execution completion, placement error and post-action settling separately rather than reporting only that the robot remained upright.
nodes.role_en: This is the deployment boundary for robot world models and policies. Claims should name the measured physical task and conditions instead of inferring complete transfer from one successful video.

Optical-axis depth differs from range along a pixel ray except on the optical axis. Simulator APIs can provide different depth conventions, clipping values and units. Lens distortion and rolling shutter require additional models when relevant. Calibration must match the image resolution and any resizing or cropping applied.
nodes.example: A point away from the optical axis has ray distance larger than its optical-axis depth. Reconstructing it with the wrong convention produces a geometric error even if the image looks correct. Check a known plane or sphere at several image locations to validate the convention.
nodes.role_en: Camera geometry supports visual observations, depth-based robot policies, world-state reconstruction and sensor simulation. It is a geometry node shared by traditional robotics and visual world models.

nodes.definition: A contact report may represent an instantaneous force, accumulated impulse, filtered value or interval aggregate depending on the engine and sensor API. Physics steps, control steps and rendering steps can have different rates. An absent reported contact is not automatically proof of no physical interaction if sampling misses a short event. Contact thresholds and coordinate frames must be stated when defining rewards or evaluating impacts.
nodes.example: A policy acts every twenty milliseconds while physics runs at five-millisecond steps. A brief contact can occur between policy observations. Determine whether the sensor reports the last substep, a maximum, an average or an accumulated quantity before using it for ball-hit success.
nodes.role_en: Contact timing connects simulator interfaces to learning rewards and evaluation. It prevents incorrect conclusions from low-rate visual captures or ambiguously aggregated force data. Document sensor aggregation and controller sampling schedules.

nodes.title: 计算复杂度
nodes.summary: Computational complexity describes how resource demand scales with problem size under an explicit cost model.
nodes.definition: Computational complexity describes how resource demand scales with problem size under an explicit cost model. Big-O is an asymptotic bound, not a hardware timing measurement. Count arithmetic operations, memory traffic and candidate evaluations separately when analysing training or planning. Vectorization can change execution efficiency without changing the mathematical operation count.
nodes.example: A planner evaluating 300 candidates for five steps invokes roughly 1,500 transition evaluations per search iteration. Batching those evaluations may reduce latency, but it does not make their arithmetic vanish. Doubling the context length of dense attention changes the pairwise-score count by approximately fourfold.
nodes.role_en: This connects planning budgets and neural-network dimensions to runtime; it prevents treating parameter count alone as inference cost.

nodes.title: 浮点数表示
nodes.summary: Floating-point formats encode a finite set of numbers using sign, exponent and significand information.
nodes.definition: Floating-point formats encode a finite set of numbers using sign, exponent and significand information. Precision and exponent range are different properties. Arithmetic rounds results and can overflow or underflow. Reordering additions can change their result because finite-precision addition is generally non-associative. Exact bit layouts and treatment of subnormals depend on the format.
nodes.example: An FP16 computation can overflow where a format with a larger exponent range does not. BF16 and FP16 both use sixteen bits, but allocate them differently. Accumulating many small values into a large total can lose the smaller contributions, motivating higher-precision accumulators for selected operations.
nodes.role_en: Training stability, mixed precision and reproducibility all depend on numeric representation; lower storage size alone does not establish equivalent numerical behaviour.

nodes.title: 张量存储、形状与步幅
nodes.summary: A tensor has logical dimensions and an underlying storage layout.
nodes.definition: A tensor has logical dimensions and an underlying storage layout. Strides map logical indices to storage locations. A view can share the same storage while changing shape or strides; a copy allocates or populates different storage. Contiguity is a layout property, not a statement that tensor values are correct. Some kernels accept arbitrary strides while others require or benefit from contiguous inputs.
nodes.example: Transposing a matrix can create a non-contiguous view without copying every element. A later contiguous conversion may allocate a copy. A pipeline that repeatedly transposes and copies can spend substantial time moving data even if the displayed matrix multiplication is efficient.
nodes.role_en: Shape-aware model implementation must also account for storage layout when predicting memory use and kernel performance.

nodes.title: 模型与训练显存估算
nodes.summary: Training memory includes parameters, gradients, optimizer states, saved activations and temporary workspaces.
nodes.definition: Training memory includes parameters, gradients, optimizer states, saved activations and temporary workspaces. Storage precision can differ among these components. Framework allocator reservations and peak overlap make observed memory differ from a simple sum. Inference may remove gradients and optimizer states but still require temporary activations, caches and workspaces.
nodes.example: One million FP32 weights require about four megabytes in decimal units. Adam commonly needs two additional moment tensors, while gradients and possibly master weights add more storage. Doubling sequence length can increase activation memory even if the parameter count is unchanged.
nodes.role_en: Use component accounting before choosing batch size, activation checkpointing or parameter sharding; GPU capacity cannot be inferred from model weights alone.

nodes.title: 并行性与阿姆达尔定律
nodes.summary: Parallel execution divides suitable work among processing resources.
nodes.definition: Parallel execution divides suitable work among processing resources. Dependencies, serial code, synchronization and data transfer limit end-to-end speedup. Amdahl’s law is a simplified upper bound with fixed workload and ideal parallel scaling. Real GPU performance also depends on memory access, occupancy and launch overhead. More parallel workers do not guarantee proportional improvement.
nodes.example: If ninety percent of a pipeline becomes ten times faster while ten percent is unchanged, the ideal overall speedup is about 5.26, not ten. A Python environment loop can limit a fast GPU policy rollout if observations are assembled serially.
nodes.role_en: This explains why faster matrix kernels or more GPUs may not proportionally accelerate a complete robotics training pipeline.

notation.meaning: Fraction of baseline execution that is parallelizable.
Ideal parallel speedup for that fraction.

nodes.title: CPU、GPU与吞吐计算
nodes.summary: A CPU is typically optimized for low-latency control and diverse execution; a GPU provides many execution resources for high-throughput parallel workloads.
nodes.definition: A CPU is typically optimized for low-latency control and diverse execution; a GPU provides many execution resources for high-throughput parallel workloads. The displayed bound separates arithmetic and data movement and ignores launch and scheduling overhead. GPU acceleration requires enough suitable parallel work and efficient data supply. Hardware details and useful performance vary by architecture.
nodes.example: A large batched matrix multiplication can expose extensive parallelism and reuse. A tiny tensor operation invoked repeatedly from Python can instead be dominated by dispatch and launch overhead. Moving inputs between CPU and GPU at every step can further reduce useful acceleration.
nodes.role_en: This is the starting point for understanding why neural-network batches and parallel simulation benefit from GPUs while some robotics control tasks remain latency-bound.

nodes.title: CUDA核函数与索引
nodes.summary: A CUDA kernel is a device function executed by a grid of thread blocks.
nodes.definition: A CUDA kernel is a device function executed by a grid of thread blocks. Each thread uses its indices to determine which data to process. The launch configuration is a logical decomposition of work, not a guarantee that all threads run simultaneously. Boundary checks prevent out-of-range accesses when the launch covers more threads than elements.
nodes.example: For a vector addition of 1,000 elements with 256 threads per block, four blocks cover 1,024 logical indices. The final twenty-four threads must skip memory accesses beyond the valid range. Multiple blocks may be scheduled at different times.
nodes.role_en: Tensor libraries invoke kernels underneath high-level operations. Understanding indexing helps explain batching, launch overhead and parallel simulation layouts.

nodes.summary: NVIDIA GPUs schedule threads in warps within streaming multiprocessors.
nodes.definition: NVIDIA GPUs schedule threads in warps within streaming multiprocessors. SIMT presents per-thread execution while grouping instruction execution across threads. Thread blocks require sufficient resources on an SM; the grid may be much larger than the simultaneously resident work. Warp width, instruction capabilities and resource limits must be read from the target architecture documentation.
nodes.example: A block of 128 threads contains four logical warps on a thirty-two-thread warp architecture. That does not mean one CUDA core executes an entire warp at once, or that all blocks are resident. Instruction issue, latency hiding and execution pipelines are separate hardware details.
nodes.role_en: This connects CUDA thread hierarchy to resource occupancy, divergence, memory access and GPU simulation throughput.

nodes.title: 分支发散
nodes.summary: Branch divergence occurs when threads grouped for SIMT execution take different control-flow paths.
nodes.definition: Branch divergence occurs when threads grouped for SIMT execution take different control-flow paths. Hardware must manage the active threads for each path, which can reduce useful execution efficiency. Predication, reconvergence and independent thread scheduling details vary. Divergence is not a correctness error by itself, and branch-free code is not always faster.
nodes.example: If neighbouring threads evaluate different collision cases, some execute one contact branch while others execute another. Reorganizing work to group similar cases may improve execution, but sorting and extra data movement can outweigh the benefit.
nodes.role_en: Contact-rich GPU simulation and irregular robot datasets may have different performance from dense neural-network arithmetic even with similar element counts.

nodes.title: GPU存储层级
nodes.summary: GPU storage includes registers, block-cooperative shared memory, caches and device memory.
nodes.definition: GPU storage includes registers, block-cooperative shared memory, caches and device memory. Scope, capacity, latency and bandwidth differ. Register and shared-memory demand can limit concurrent work. Cache behaviour and memory technology are architecture-specific. A logical tensor being on the GPU does not mean every access is served from its fastest storage.
nodes.example: A matrix multiplication tile can reuse values loaded into shared memory rather than repeatedly fetching them from device memory. Excessive per-thread registers may reduce residency or cause spilling, increasing memory traffic. The best tile size therefore balances several resource constraints.
nodes.role_en: The hierarchy explains why data reuse, tiling and fusion can matter as much as the number of arithmetic operations.

notation.meaning: Thread-local fast storage, subject to resource limits.

nodes.title: 合并访存
nodes.summary: Coalescing combines suitable memory accesses from threads into efficient memory transactions.
nodes.definition: Coalescing combines suitable memory accesses from threads into efficient memory transactions. Consecutive addresses, alignment and access width influence transaction count. Strided, scattered or poorly aligned accesses can transfer unused bytes and lower effective bandwidth. Exact transaction rules depend on the GPU generation and memory instruction. Coalescing is a property of accesses, not simply tensor shape.
nodes.example: Threads reading adjacent FP32 elements can use memory transactions efficiently. If neighbouring threads instead read widely separated rows, the same number of requested values can require more transactions. A transpose may require a tiled access strategy to make both reads and writes efficient.
nodes.role_en: Robot observation layouts, image processing and custom CUDA kernels benefit from matching parallel thread indexing to storage layout.

notation.meaning: Bytes per element for contiguous accesses.

nodes.title: 分块矩阵乘法
nodes.summary: Tiling partitions matrix multiplication into reusable subproblems.
nodes.definition: Tiling partitions matrix multiplication into reusable subproblems. A block computes an output tile while reusing input tiles across multiple products. This reduces traffic per useful arithmetic operation relative to repeatedly loading each operand. Tile dimensions interact with shared memory, registers, Tensor Core instructions and scheduling. High throughput requires suitable shapes and efficient handling of boundary tiles.
nodes.example: An input value used in several output dot products can be loaded once into cooperative storage and reused. A small matrix-vector multiplication may have much less reuse than a large matrix-matrix multiplication, so equal nominal FLOP rates do not imply equal achievable speed.
nodes.role_en: Dense layers, attention projections and simulation linear algebra rely on the same matrix multiplication principles.

notation.meaning: Multiply-and-add operation count under the usual convention.

nodes.explain: Tiling partitions matrix multiplication into reusable subproblems. A block computes an output tile while reusing input tiles across multiple products. nodes.title: Tensor Core与矩阵指令
nodes.summary: Tensor Cores execute supported matrix operations using architecture-dependent operand formats, shapes and accumulation behaviour.
nodes.definition: Tensor Cores execute supported matrix operations using architecture-dependent operand formats, shapes and accumulation behaviour. They are not interchangeable with every ordinary CUDA execution unit. Frameworks and libraries select suitable kernels when data types, dimensions and hardware allow. Nominal peak throughput assumes favourable conditions and is not an end-to-end application speed measurement.
nodes.example: A mixed-precision dense layer may use matrix instructions with lower-precision operands and higher-precision accumulation. A scalar branch-heavy environment update may use ordinary instructions instead. Changing model dtype does not guarantee all operations use Tensor Cores or preserve numerical accuracy.
nodes.role_en: This explains a major source of training throughput while clarifying why robot simulation, attention and optimizer steps can have different bottlenecks.

notation.meaning: Small matrix fragments processed by a supported matrix instruction.

nodes.title: 数学库与算子分派
nodes.summary: A high-level tensor operation passes through framework dispatch to an implementation appropriate for device, dtype, layout and other conditions.
nodes.definition: A high-level tensor operation passes through framework dispatch to an implementation appropriate for device, dtype, layout and other conditions. Backends may use vendor libraries or generated/custom kernels. The mapping is not always one Python call to one kernel, especially under compilation or fusion. Backend selection can change with software versions and input properties.
nodes.example: A PyTorch matrix product on CUDA can dispatch to an optimized matrix backend rather than execute a Python loop over entries. Adjacent elementwise operations may still launch separate kernels in eager mode unless another optimization combines them.
nodes.role_en: This connects the mathematical model description to the actual GPU work executed during training and inference.

nodes.title: 反向自动微分与向量雅可比积
nodes.summary: Reverse-mode automatic differentiation propagates vector-Jacobian products through recorded operations.
nodes.definition: Reverse-mode automatic differentiation propagates vector-Jacobian products through recorded operations. It can compute gradients of a scalar loss with respect to many parameters without explicitly materializing every Jacobian. Backward requires relevant forward values or recomputation. Differentiability and numerical correctness of local operations still matter; autograd does not validate a model’s physical predictions.
nodes.example: For a large matrix layer, backward can compute parameter and input gradients using matrix products rather than constructing a huge dense Jacobian. Detaching the next state in an imagined rollout breaks gradient propagation across that transition, even though the forward numbers remain available.
nodes.role_en: SuperMimic-style policy optimization needs gradients through learned transition rollouts. This is different from using CEM with fixed, derivative-free model evaluation.

notation.meaning: Incoming sensitivity of a scalar objective to y.

nodes.en: Dynamic Autograd Graphs and Saved Tensors
nodes.title: 动态自动微分图与保存张量
nodes.summary: PyTorch eager autograd records executed tensor operations needed for gradient computation.
nodes.definition: PyTorch eager autograd records executed tensor operations needed for gradient computation. Saved forward values and graph references affect memory lifetime. Creating tensors without gradients, detaching values or using inference modes changes what is recorded. Graph retention and higher-order differentiation can require additional memory and different API settings.
nodes.example: Saving a training loss tensor to a long-lived Python list can retain graph references unless only a detached scalar is stored. Accumulating unintended references can increase memory consumption even when the model shape is unchanged.
nodes.role_en: Understanding graph lifetime helps debug differentiable rollouts, memory growth and accidental gradient breaks in learned world models.

nodes.en: Devices, Allocation and the Caching Allocator
nodes.title: 设备、显存分配与缓存分配器
nodes.summary: CUDA tensors have a device and storage allocation.
nodes.definition: CUDA tensors have a device and storage allocation. PyTorch commonly caches device memory to reduce allocation overhead, so reserved memory can exceed currently allocated live tensors. External libraries and driver usage add other accounting. Deleting a tensor reference, freeing unused cache and reducing peak working memory are different actions. Device placement must be consistent across participating operations.
nodes.example: A tensor can be released while its block remains reserved for reuse, so a process-level GPU monitor may not immediately show a drop. Calling an empty-cache function does not free live tensors or make an oversized training batch fit without other changes.
nodes.role_en: This supports interpreting GPU memory statistics without assuming every reservation is a leak. It also explains out-of-memory failures and device mismatch errors.

notation.meaning: Memory occupied by live tensor allocations in the selected accounting.
Memory held by the allocator from the device.

nodes.title: CUDA流、事件与异步执行
nodes.summary: CUDA launches are often asynchronous relative to host execution.
nodes.definition: CUDA launches are often asynchronous relative to host execution. Operations are ordered within a stream; cross-stream dependencies need appropriate coordination. Host enqueue time is not device completion time. Events or explicit synchronization establish suitable timing boundaries. Excessive synchronization can destroy overlap, while missing dependencies can cause incorrect reads or writes.
nodes.example: A Python timer placed immediately around a CUDA operation may measure mostly launch overhead. Recording device events and waiting for completion can measure GPU work more accurately. A transfer and compute operation can overlap only when hardware, memory and dependency conditions permit.
nodes.role_en: Correct timing is necessary for comparing planners, simulations and training pipelines; asynchronous launch is not evidence that a result is already computed.

notation.meaning: Ordered sequence of operations on a device.

nodes.title: 数据加载、锁页内存与传输
nodes.summary: Training input pipelines include storage reads, decoding, augmentation, batching and transfer.
nodes.definition: Training input pipelines include storage reads, decoding, augmentation, batching and transfer. Worker processes can overlap CPU preparation; pinned host memory can support suitable asynchronous transfers. More workers or pinned buffers can increase memory demand and contention. Effective overlap depends on queueing, synchronization and whether preprocessing itself is the bottleneck.
nodes.example: If image decoding takes twice as long as GPU computation, faster matrix kernels alone may not improve training throughput. Precomputing frozen features can change the bottleneck, but only if it preserves the intended augmentation and experimental protocol.
nodes.role_en: Robot video datasets often need careful input-pipeline design before additional GPU capacity produces useful speedup.

nodes.role: Robot video datasets often need careful input-pipeline design before additional GPU capacity produces useful speedup.

nodes.title: 批处理与梯度累积
nodes.summary: Batching groups examples for efficient tensor operations.
nodes.definition: Batching groups examples for efficient tensor operations. Gradient accumulation sums or averages gradients over microbatches before updating parameters. Effective batch size depends on the loss normalization and distributed sampling. Accumulation is not always identical to one large batch because dropout, normalization, clipping and stochastic data transformations can differ.
nodes.example: Four microbatches of sixteen examples on two data-parallel workers correspond to 128 examples per update if gradients are normalized consistently. Calling the optimizer step after each microbatch changes the update sequence and is a different experiment.
nodes.role_en: This links statistical training choices to GPU utilization and memory limits, especially for large video or action models.

notation.meaning: Data-parallel workers under the stated sampling protocol.

nodes.title: 自动混合精度
nodes.summary: Mixed-precision training selects lower precision for suitable operations while keeping other calculations in higher precision.
nodes.definition: Mixed-precision training selects lower precision for suitable operations while keeping other calculations in higher precision. Autocast chooses operation dtypes; gradient scaling addresses selected underflow risks and is not universally required for every lower-precision format. Stability, speed and memory benefits depend on model, backend and hardware. Precision changes must be validated against the objective and task outcomes.
nodes.example: A matrix multiplication may use a lower-precision path while a reduction remains higher precision. FP16 gradient scaling can prevent small gradients from underflowing, but cannot correct every source of unstable training or bad data. BF16 has different range and precision tradeoffs.
nodes.role_en: This explains practical acceleration of large world models and VLAs without equating reduced precision to guaranteed equal accuracy.

notation.meaning: Loss-scaling factor when scaling is used.

nodes.title: 激活重计算
nodes.summary: Activation checkpointing saves a selected subset of forward intermediates and recomputes others during backward.
nodes.definition: Activation checkpointing saves a selected subset of forward intermediates and recomputes others during backward. It trades additional computation for lower activation memory. It is different from saving training state to disk. Correctness requires recomputation behaviour compatible with the chosen checkpointing method, randomness and side effects. The benefit depends on which layers dominate peak memory.
nodes.example: Checkpointing a stack of Transformer blocks can permit a longer context at the cost of repeated forward work. It does not reduce parameter or optimizer-state storage in the same way that parameter sharding does. Wall-clock impact must be measured.
nodes.role_en: This is a common memory technique for video diffusion and long imagined rollouts; it changes runtime without reducing the mathematical model depth.

notation.meaning: Intermediate value needed for a backward rule.
Selected boundary from which intermediates are recomputed.

nodes.role: This is a common memory technique for video diffusion and long imagined rollouts; it changes runtime without reducing the mathematical model depth.

nodes.title: 分布式数据并行与全归约
nodes.summary: Data parallelism replicates the model across workers and computes gradients on different data shards.
nodes.definition: Data parallelism replicates the model across workers and computes gradients on different data shards. Collective communication combines corresponding gradients so synchronized replicas perform consistent updates. DDP can overlap communication with backward using gradient buckets. Speedup depends on compute, communication, batch size and imbalance; distributed correctness also requires consistent model and data handling.
nodes.example: Two workers process different examples, then average their gradients before an update. If one worker receives a much slower input batch, the other may wait during synchronization. Doubling worker count can change effective batch size unless other settings are adjusted.
nodes.role_en: This is the systems layer beneath multi-GPU paper training reports. Report GPU-hours and wall-clock time separately and document the effective batch.

nodes.title: 参数、梯度与优化器分片
nodes.summary: Sharding distributes selected model states across workers rather than keeping all states replicated.
nodes.definition: Sharding distributes selected model states across workers rather than keeping all states replicated. Different strategies shard optimizer state, gradients, parameters or combinations. Execution may gather parameters temporarily and introduce communication. Persistent memory reduction does not directly specify peak memory, throughput or inference behaviour. Framework versions and wrapping choices affect actual execution.
nodes.example: A large model can fit across several workers because each stores only part of its persistent states. During a layer computation, gathered weights and activation buffers can still produce a peak much larger than the simple one-over-worker-count estimate.
nodes.role_en: This supports reading large-model training configurations and distinguishing memory scaling from data-parallel throughput scaling.

notation.meaning: Persistent per-worker storage, excluding temporary gathered states.

nodes.title: 图捕获、编译与融合
nodes.summary: Compilation captures supported program regions and transforms their tensor operations into optimized implementations.
nodes.definition: Compilation captures supported program regions and transforms their tensor operations into optimized implementations. Fusion may reduce intermediate storage and kernel-launch overhead. Dynamic control flow, unsupported operations and shape changes can cause graph breaks or recompilation. Compilation startup cost and steady-state performance must be separated. Compiling a program does not change its task specification or guarantee a speedup.
nodes.example: A sequence of elementwise activations and arithmetic may become fewer kernels, whereas an already efficient matrix multiplication may remain a library call. Benchmark after the intended warmup and include compilation cost when it matters for a short-lived job.
nodes.role_en: This connects high-level PyTorch code to generated GPU execution and helps explain version- and shape-dependent training speed.

notation.meaning: Combining operations to reduce launches or intermediate traffic.
A boundary where execution cannot remain in the compiled graph.

nodes.explain: Compilation captures supported program regions and transforms their tensor operations into optimized implementations. Fusion may reduce intermediate storage and kernel-launch overhead. Compiling a program does not change its task specification or guarantee a speedup.
nodes.role: This connects high-level PyTorch code to generated GPU execution and helps explain version- and shape-dependent training speed.

nodes.title: Triton与自定义GPU核函数
nodes.summary: Triton is a language and compiler for writing GPU kernels with tensor-oriented operations and explicit memory access patterns.
nodes.definition: Triton is a language and compiler for writing GPU kernels with tensor-oriented operations and explicit memory access patterns. It can express tiled computation and is used by compiler backends and custom operators. Correctness, masks, layout and resource use still require attention. A custom kernel is valuable only when it improves a relevant measured bottleneck while preserving required numerical behaviour.
nodes.example: A fused operation can load a tile, apply several elementwise transforms and write once instead of storing every intermediate. For an unusual shape, an optimized library kernel may still be faster than a simple custom implementation. Validate both output and timing.
nodes.role_en: This is an optional advanced branch for training-system optimization, not a prerequisite for understanding a world-model paper’s mathematical method.

notation.meaning: Block of logical tensor elements handled by a program instance.

nodes.explain: Triton is a language and compiler for writing GPU kernels with tensor-oriented operations and explicit memory access patterns. It can express tiled computation and is used by compiler backends and custom operators. Correctness, masks, layout and resource use still require attention. nodes.title: FlashAttention与IO感知注意力
nodes.summary: FlashAttention reorganizes exact attention computation using tiling and numerically stable blockwise normalization to reduce memory traffic.
nodes.definition: FlashAttention reorganizes exact attention computation using tiling and numerically stable blockwise normalization to reduce memory traffic. It does not replace attention with an arbitrary approximate sparse pattern. Arithmetic complexity, memory footprint and wall-clock time are distinct quantities. Supported variants and precision behaviour depend on implementation. IO-aware algorithms exploit the GPU hierarchy rather than merely adding more compute units.
nodes.example: Ordinary attention can materialize a sequence-by-sequence score matrix. Tiled attention processes blocks while maintaining normalization information, avoiding full score storage in high-bandwidth memory. Speed benefits depend on sequence length, dimensions and hardware rather than a universal acceleration factor.
nodes.role_en: This connects the attention formula to efficient large-model training and explains why a mathematical operation can stay the same while its implementation becomes much faster.
nodes.latex: Y=\operatorname{softmax}(QK^\top/\sqrt{d_k})V\quad\text{without storing the full score matrix in device memory}

It does not replace attention with an arbitrary approximate sparse pattern. Arithmetic complexity, memory footprint and wall-clock time are distinct quantities. nodes.title: 性能分析与Roofline模型
nodes.summary: Profiling records time and resource use to locate a workload’s actual bottleneck.
nodes.definition: Profiling records time and resource use to locate a workload’s actual bottleneck. The roofline model relates arithmetic intensity to compute and memory ceilings as a simplified performance guide. Kernel launches, synchronization, CPU work and communication can create additional limits. A utilization percentage alone does not reveal which change will improve end-to-end throughput.
nodes.example: A bandwidth-limited optimizer kernel may benefit more from reduced memory traffic than additional matrix throughput. A small inference loop can be launch-bound. Compare both kernel traces and complete-step timing before deciding whether to fuse operations, increase batching or optimize input loading.
nodes.role_en: This supports evidence-based optimization of robot training, world-model rollouts and planning latency rather than attributing all speed differences to network depth.

notation.meaning: Arithmetic intensity: operations per transferred byte.
Relevant compute ceiling under the stated precision.

nodes.title: 随机种子、确定性与实验复现
nodes.summary: Reproducibility requires recording data, code, configuration, software, hardware and randomness.
nodes.definition: Reproducibility requires recording data, code, configuration, software, hardware and randomness. Setting one seed does not guarantee identical results across devices, versions, parallel schedules or nondeterministic kernels. Deterministic settings can change available algorithms and performance. Repeated seeds measure variation in a protocol; they do not automatically establish generalization to unseen environments.
nodes.example: A training run resumed without restoring the optimizer, scheduler and random states may follow a different trajectory even if model weights match. Exact numerical replication and statistically similar task performance are different evaluation goals.
nodes.role_en: This provides a shared foundation for comparing robotics papers and deciding what a reproduction result actually establishes.

notation.meaning: Complete experimental procedure, not only the neural network.
Initial state of selected pseudo-random generators.

nodes.title: 训练检查点与恢复状态
nodes.summary: A training checkpoint stores selected state needed to restart computation.
nodes.definition: A training checkpoint stores selected state needed to restart computation. Saving weights alone supports loading a model but may not reproduce the original training continuation. Optimizer moments, schedules, random generators, data sampler state and step counters can matter. Disk checkpointing is distinct from activation recomputation, which changes how backward intermediates are stored.
nodes.example: Restoring Adam weights without its moment estimates changes subsequent updates. A robot policy file can be sufficient for inference yet insufficient to resume a training experiment or establish the identity of the data used to produce it.
nodes.role_en: This distinguishes downloadable model assets, reproducible training state and completed evaluation evidence across world-model and policy projects.

notation.meaning: Serialized training state under a chosen resume protocol.

nodes.explain: A training checkpoint stores selected state needed to restart computation. Saving weights alone supports loading a model but may not reproduce the original training continuation. nodes.role: This distinguishes downloadable model assets, reproducible training state and completed evaluation evidence across world-model and policy projects.

nodes.en: Drivers, CUDA Runtime and Package Environments
nodes.title: 驱动、CUDA运行时与软件环境
nodes.summary: GPU software has multiple layers: application packages, compiled extensions, runtimes, numerical libraries, drivers and hardware.
nodes.definition: GPU software has multiple layers: application packages, compiled extensions, runtimes, numerical libraries, drivers and hardware. Compatible version ranges are not equivalent to identical versions. A framework wheel can bundle selected libraries while depending on an installed driver. Installing a toolkit does not automatically rebuild every extension or change the libraries an existing process uses.
nodes.example: A package can import successfully yet fail when launching its first kernel because an extension was built for an unsupported target or incompatible runtime. Record the actual environment and test representative operations rather than treating installation completion as training validation.
nodes.role_en: This connects compute architecture to practical environment setup and explains why simulation and training stacks need explicit compatibility checks.

notation.meaning: Host software controlling the GPU and providing supported interfaces.

nodes.explain: GPU software has multiple layers: application packages, compiled extensions, runtimes, numerical libraries, drivers and hardware. Compatible version ranges are not equivalent to identical versions. A framework wheel can bundle selected libraries while depending on an installed driver. Installing a toolkit does not automatically rebuild every extension or change the libraries an existing process uses.
nodes.role: This connects compute architecture to practical environment setup and explains why simulation and training stacks need explicit compatibility checks.

nodes.title: 世界模型：表征、动态与控制
nodes.summary: Factor vision, temporal modeling and action selection into separate trainable components.
nodes.definition: World Models separates visual compression, temporal prediction and control. A variational autoencoder maps an image to a latent vector. A recurrent mixture-density model predicts future latent distributions conditioned on actions and memory. A compact controller uses these features to select actions. The experiments investigate whether policies can exploit a learned internal model, including training a Doom policy in a generated environment. This is a historically important learned-model design, rather than a claim that every task can be solved in an imagined environment.
nodes.example: For a racing image, first obtain a visual latent and update recurrent memory using the previous action. The controller outputs steering and acceleration from those features. In the separate Doom experiment, policy training occurs inside the learned model. These two protocols must not be merged into a single statement that all reported controllers were trained entirely in imagination.
nodes.role_en: This foundational example connects VAE representations, recurrent dynamics, uncertainty and controller learning. Its game experiments motivate robot modeling concepts, but are not themselves robot-hardware validation.

nodes.title: 从像素学习潜在动力学并规划
nodes.summary: Learn probabilistic latent dynamics for online planning directly from image observations.
nodes.definition: PlaNet learns image-based dynamics and selects actions through online planning in latent space. Its recurrent state-space model combines deterministic memory with stochastic state, allowing uncertainty and information from past observations to coexist. Image and reward reconstruction train the model, while latent overshooting encourages predictions over multiple time steps. At action selection, candidate sequences are evaluated in this learned state space. Unlike a direct policy that returns an action in one network call, PlaNet repeatedly uses trajectory optimization to choose a plan.
nodes.example: From a camera observation of a simulated walker, infer the current latent state. Sample candidate motor sequences, predict their latent trajectories and rewards, and retain promising sequences with CEM. Execute part of the best plan, obtain a new image and repeat. The decoder helps training but need not render every candidate image during planning.
nodes.role_en: PlaNet is a key bridge from probabilistic state-space modeling to learned visual MPC. Its RSSM and planning/acting distinction support understanding later imagination-based agents.

paper.training: Train observation/reward prediction and latent consistency from interaction data, including latent overshooting.
paper.inference: Infer latent state and run CEM inside a receding-horizon control loop.
paper.evaluation: Pixel-based continuous-control tasks from DeepMind Control.
paper.scale: Training and planning costs differ; exact model count is not normalized in this atlas.
paper.limitations: Model bias grows over long rollouts; latent reward predictions can be wrong under unusual actions.

nodes.title: 通过潜在想象学习控制策略
nodes.summary: Learn behavior through latent imagination rather than only online action-sequence search.
nodes.definition: Dreamer learns a latent dynamics model from observations and then trains an actor and a value function using imagined trajectories. The actor can receive gradients through differentiable latent transitions, which helps optimize behavior over a longer effective horizon than directly searching a long raw action sequence. A learned value function supplies estimates beyond a finite imagined rollout. The distinction is structural: the world model is learned from experience, while the behavior is improved inside that model and then used to collect or execute real environment actions.
nodes.example: Infer a latent state from the current camera frame. Starting at that state, unroll several model transitions using the actor, predict rewards and bootstrap the remaining return with the value model. Update the actor using those imagined outcomes. At environment time, action selection uses the actor instead of rerunning a full CEM search for every decision.
nodes.role_en: Dreamer links backpropagation through time, latent probabilistic modeling and actor-critic training. It provides a useful contrast to ID-WM, which searches for goal-reaching decisions at inference.

notation.meaning: Terminal value estimate. The equation is a conceptual return objective.

paper.inference: Infer state and run the learned actor; model-based training does not require image generation for each executed action.

nodes.summary: Use discrete stochastic states and training stabilization to extend imagination-based learning to Atari.
nodes.definition: DreamerV2 develops the Dreamer recipe using categorical latent variables and stabilized world-model and behavior learning. Stochastic latent categories are sampled while straight-through gradients provide an approximate differentiable path. KL balancing separates the pressure applied to prior and posterior distributions. The model learns from environment experience and trains behavior through imagined states. Its Atari results establish a particular sample-efficient game-learning capability; they do not automatically imply accurate continuous robot contact dynamics or unrestricted transfer to other embodiments.
nodes.example: An image encoder infers categorical latent state from an Atari frame. The prior predicts the next distribution without seeing the future image; the posterior uses the next image during training. KL-related losses align them. An actor learns from rollouts under the prior, so prior errors matter even if posterior reconstructions look accurate.
nodes.role_en: This paper connects categorical random variables, approximate gradients and probabilistic model training. It clarifies why latent distribution design is a separate architectural choice from action or policy representation.

nodes.summary: Stabilize the Dreamer learning system for broad task diversity with a shared recipe.
nodes.definition: DreamerV3 targets an imagination-based reinforcement-learning algorithm that remains effective across diverse observation spaces, action types and reward scales. It retains the recurrent stochastic world model, actor and critic, while introducing normalization and prediction choices such as symlog transforms, distributional targets and balanced regularization. These changes reduce per-domain retuning in the reported evaluation. The work should be understood as a robust training system whose components interact, not as a single new dynamics-layer architecture or a universal proof of generalization.
nodes.example: Consider one task with tiny rewards and another with much larger returns. A fixed raw regression loss can put them on incompatible numerical scales. DreamerV3 transforms targets and normalizes behavior-learning signals so the same algorithm settings can be tested more broadly. Performance still depends on training interaction, task construction and model capacity.
nodes.role_en: This is the modern Dreamer-family reference for stable model-based RL. It connects numerical scaling and distributional prediction to practical training, including robotics-like continuous-control benchmarks.

nodes.title: 时序差分学习与模型预测控制
nodes.summary: Combine local model-based optimization and temporal-difference terminal values.
nodes.definition: TD-MPC combines short-horizon latent trajectory optimization with a learned terminal value estimate. Its task-oriented latent dynamics model is trained jointly with reward and value components, rather than being required to reconstruct every image detail. The planner uses local modeled rewards and the terminal value to evaluate candidate action sequences. Temporal-difference learning supplies long-range reward information. This differs from reward-free goal-distance planning: the latent space is shaped by the task and its return-prediction objective.
nodes.example: For a reaching task, compare several short motor sequences using predicted rewards. At the end of each short rollout, add the learned value of the predicted terminal state. A sequence that is initially indirect can still score well if its terminal value predicts future progress beyond the rollout horizon.
nodes.role_en: TD-MPC illustrates how value learning compensates for limited model horizon. It is an important comparison branch for understanding what ID-WM gains or avoids by using goal-driven subgoals instead of task values.

notation.meaning: Learned reward prediction. This is a conceptual planner score.

paper.training: Train latent dynamics, rewards and value functions from interaction/replay.
paper.inference: Optimize short sequences, execute and replan with terminal value estimates.
paper.evaluation: DMControl and Meta-World state/image continuous-control tasks.
paper.scale: Model dimensions and planning candidate budgets are separate quantities.
paper.limitations: Task-shaped latents depend on reward coverage; learned values can also be exploited.

nodes.summary: Scale and stabilize latent MPC across tasks, embodiments and model sizes.
nodes.definition: TD-MPC2 improves the TD-MPC learning and planning system for robustness across many continuous-control tasks. It keeps decoder-free latent dynamics and terminal-value-guided local optimization, while changing representation constraints, value-learning design and training stabilization. The work studies larger models and multi-task training with different embodiments and action spaces. Its reported shared-hyperparameter performance is evidence within a specified benchmark collection; it is not equivalent to a model that controls arbitrary unseen robots without data or calibration.
nodes.example: A multi-task training batch may contain trajectories from different control problems. A task-conditioned representation identifies which dynamics and reward objective apply, while shared network capacity captures reusable structure. Planning still uses the task context and admissible action dimensions, rather than interpreting all tasks as one identical action space.
nodes.role_en: TD-MPC2 connects model/data scaling to model-based continuous control. It complements JEPA-style reward-free representations by showing a task-oriented latent world-model route.

nodes.title: 图像联合嵌入预测架构
nodes.summary: Predict semantic image-region embeddings from context without pixel reconstruction or negative pairs.
nodes.definition: I-JEPA learns image representations by predicting target-region features from visible context-region features. The target branch encodes the image and supplies stop-gradient representation targets; a predictor uses context and target-position information. Large target blocks and informative distributed context encourage semantic prediction rather than merely interpolating nearby pixel texture. The objective predicts representations rather than reconstructing pixels or contrasting against a set of negative examples. This is a representation-learning paper, not yet an action-conditioned robot dynamics model.
nodes.example: Hide several image blocks while leaving spatially distributed context visible. The context encoder and predictor estimate the target encoder features at the hidden positions. Matching these vectors trains useful image features. No robot action enters this image-only training example, so a controller cannot obtain motor consequences merely by running the encoder.
nodes.role_en: I-JEPA provides the representation-prediction foundation for later video JEPAs and action-conditioned predictive models. It should remain distinct from the full control loop.

nodes.title: 视频特征预测自监督学习
nodes.summary: Learn video representations using masked feature prediction alone.
nodes.definition: V-JEPA extends feature prediction to masked spatiotemporal regions in video. A context encoder sees visible video tokens; a predictor estimates target representations computed by a separate target encoder. Training does not require action labels, text, negative examples or pixel reconstruction. The resulting representation is evaluated through downstream video and image tasks, including motion-sensitive recognition. Video representation learning can support later world modeling, but this action-free objective should not be presented as an executable robot controller or an explicit action-conditioned simulator.
nodes.example: Take a short video of an object moving across a table and mask blocks across space and time. The model predicts features at those positions from the remaining clip. It can learn motion-related structure without producing the missing RGB frames. Predicting features from a partially visible clip is also not identical to always predicting strictly future frames.
nodes.role_en: This is the original video-JEPA paper, linking temporal tokenization, positional encoding and self-supervised target prediction. Action-conditioned planning is introduced in later extensions.

paper.inference: Use frozen or adapted encoder features in downstream tasks.

paper.limitations: No action-conditioned motor transition is learned solely from these unlabeled clips.

nodes.summary: Learn representation-space effects of controlled image transformations beyond masking.
nodes.definition: Image World Models generalize representation prediction beyond masked-image completion. A predictor learns the effect of specified image transformations in feature space, including global photometric changes. The paper studies how conditioning, prediction difficulty and predictor capacity affect learned representations. By controlling which changes are predicted or ignored, the method explores invariance and equivariance. Here the term world model refers to learned transformation behavior in visual representations; it must not be interpreted as a demonstrated robot forward dynamics model with actuator inputs.
nodes.example: Create two views of one image with a known color transformation. The model receives a source representation and transformation information and predicts the target representation. Features can preserve transformation-related information when the task requires predicting it, rather than discarding every augmentation effect. This helps distinguish invariant and equivariant representation objectives.

nodes.summary: Learn a compact JEPA world model from pixels using prediction and a Gaussian anti-collapse regularizer.
nodes.definition: LeWorldModel learns an action-conditioned latent world model end to end from raw pixels. A next-embedding prediction term is combined with a regularizer that encourages Gaussian-distributed latent embeddings, addressing representation collapse without a pretrained frozen visual encoder. A lightweight learned representation and predictor are then used for latent-space planning. The paper separates planning results from probing latent physical quantities and violation-of-expectation diagnostics. Those probes measure specific properties and should not be promoted into a universal claim of physical understanding.
nodes.example: Encode an image, predict its future embedding from an action sequence, and compare the prediction with the encoded future training frame. At inference, CEM searches actions using the learned latent distance.
nodes.role_en: LeWM contrasts end-to-end representation learning with frozen DINO-WM features. It is useful for studying the tradeoff between small task-trained models, representation collapse control and planning quality.

nodes.summary: Decouple programmable state transitions and persistent state from generative visual realization.
nodes.definition: PWM separates explicit world-state evolution from video observation generation. A coding agent translates instructions into executable rules, and a lightweight runtime maintains entity state, including off-screen or nonvisual attributes. State-augmented three-dimensional oriented bounding boxes provide an editable geometric interface. A compiler projects state into spatial and temporal controls for a pretrained video renderer. The architecture aims at persistent, programmable generative environments. It does not establish that a visually plausible observation is a precise physical simulation or that generation outperforms a conventional renderer in runtime.
nodes.example: Define a character position, health and alive flag in code. A hit event changes health, while the visual renderer is conditioned to show the corresponding outcome. Looking away need not erase the stored state. The explicit state update can be exact with respect to the program, while the generated pixels can still fail to express it correctly.
nodes.role_en: PWM connects symbolic/program state, coarse geometry and large video models. It is an adjacent generative-environment design for robotics, not a direct replacement for validated contact dynamics.

nodes.summary: Separate executable world evolution from proxy-conditioned video rendering.
nodes.definition: Code World Model uses executable code to maintain an evolving world and a video model to produce detailed observations. A lightweight compiler renders coarse proxy geometry, which connects explicit state to frame-aligned video conditioning. The prototype builds on existing game-engine code for controls, collision handling and update logic. The video renderer is adapted with LoRA. This separation improves direct scene and motion control, while leaving substantial generative cost. The paper explicitly does not implement autoregressive real-time generation or autonomously construct a complete open-world simulator.
nodes.example: A coding agent changes object positions and gameplay state in an executable scene. The engine produces a low-resolution proxy sequence with camera motion, semantic IDs and depth. The adapted video model turns that proxy into a detailed sequence. A 24-FPS output video specifies playback time; it does not show that inference generated twenty-four frames per second.

nodes.definition: GigaWorld-0 is designed as a data engine for vision-language-action learning. Its video component generates diverse appearance-rich embodied sequences with controls over viewpoint and action semantics. Its three-dimensional component combines generative geometry, reconstruction, system identification and executable motion planning to add geometric and physical structure. nodes.explain: GigaWorld-0 is designed as a data engine for vision-language-action learning. Its video component generates diverse appearance-rich embodied sequences with controls over viewpoint and action semantics. Its three-dimensional component combines generative geometry, reconstruction, system identification and executable motion planning to add geometric and physical structure. The framework targets instruction-aligned interaction data rather than merely attractive videos. Synthetic-data quality is evaluated partly through downstream robot policies, which must be kept distinct from direct world-model physical accuracy.

nodes.role: This paper connects video generation, geometric simulation and VLA data scaling. It is the precise GigaWorld-0 work, not a generic label for every GigaAI world-model release.

nodes.title: 面向机器人策略评估的世界模型
nodes.summary: Optimize world-model rollout consistency for agreement with real robot policy evaluation.
nodes.definition: GigaWorld-1 studies learned world models as surrogate evaluators of robot policies. It introduces matched real-policy and generated rollouts through WMBench, then analyzes action encodings, data mixtures, memory and long-horizon consistency. The final model uses control signals suitable for static head and moving wrist views, together with hierarchical visual history and persistent appearance context. The target is agreement with real policy outcomes, not simply short-term image realism. A surrogate evaluator still requires real-world calibration and held-out validation.
nodes.example: Two manipulation policies can produce videos that look equally sharp while differing in whether the gripper actually follows the commanded action. Compare generated rollouts against matched real executions and measure whether the world model ranks the policies consistently. Wrist-camera motion also requires explicit camera information to avoid confusing viewpoint changes with object movement.
nodes.role_en: This paper turns evaluation reliability into a world-model design objective. It connects geometry-aware action conditioning and memory to the practical question of whether simulator-based policy assessment can be trusted.

nodes.definition: Cosmos presents an open platform of world foundation models, video tokenizers and data-processing tools for physical-AI development. Its generative models can be customized using domain data for robotics and autonomous systems. The platform distinguishes autoregressive and diffusion modeling routes rather than reducing all world modeling to one objective. It is infrastructure for constructing and adapting learned simulators and synthetic-data pipelines. A general pretrained video prior is not automatically an action-faithful environment for a particular robot or a verified replacement for a rigid-body engine.
nodes.example: Start with a pretrained video world model and adapt its conditioning to robot interaction data. A simulation or geometry pipeline can supply controls while the model provides varied visual realization. Before evaluating policies in the model, test action responsiveness and long-horizon outcome agreement on held-out robot trajectories.
